papers.title: Energy-Latency Trade-offs in O-RAN with Distributed Baseband Processing and AI Inference
papers.authors: Urooj Tariq, Rishu Raj, Shashi Raj Pandey, Merim Dzaferagic, Petar Popovski, Dan Kilper
papers.abstract: The Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) architecture introduces flexible functional splits and open interfaces that enable distributed and centralized deployment of baseband processing. While this flexibility offers opportunities for improved resource utilization, it also introduces fundamental trade-offs between energy efficiency and latency. In this paper, we develop a throughput-based end-to-end energy consumption model for O-RAN and extend it by incorporating detailed latency modeling and application-specific Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning inference costs. The proposed end-to-end modeling framework provides a general representation of processing, transport, and inference-related energy and delay across the access, metro, and long-haul network segments. Building on this general model, we formulate an optimization problem that selects the placement of baseband processing and AI inference tasks across candidate O-RAN configurations to analyze energy-latency tradeoffs under network load, server frequency, and energy-budget constraints. Using representative hardware platforms and realistic traffic assumptions, we evaluate multiple baseband processing placements corresponding to different O-RAN functional configurations. Our results reveal how user quality of service requirements and network load conditions jointly determine the optimal placement of baseband processing and AI inference tasks, highlighting the inherent trade-off between energy efficiency and latency. The analysis provides practical insights for latency-aware and energy-efficient O-RAN deployments supporting emerging AI-driven services.
papers.summary_cn: 本文构建了O-RAN端到端能耗-延迟联合模型，涵盖接入、城域与长途网段，并将AI/ML推理开销纳入建模范围。通过优化基带处理与推理任务在O-RAN功能分割中的部署位置，分析了能效与延迟之间的权衡关系。结果表明，最优部署策略取决于用户QoS需求与网络负载条件，为AI驱动的O-RAN部署提供了实际指导。

strengths: Comprehensive end-to-end energy-latency model incorporating AI inference costs
Practical optimization framework for baseband and AI task placement
Useful insights for O-RAN deployment decisions under QoS constraints
limitations: Model-based analysis without empirical validation on real hardware
Simplified traffic assumptions may not capture real-world variability
Limited exploration of edge cases and failure scenarios
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Uses representative hardware power models and realistic traffic assumptions, but entirely simulation-based without experimental validation on actual O-RAN deployments
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Competent modeling paper with practical relevance, but lacks the empirical grounding and novelty to stand out; incremental contribution to well-studied energy-latency trade-off space

papers.title: Embodied Passive Aeroacoustic Perception Enables Relative Sensing and Pursuit Between Aerial Robots
papers.authors: Yanbaihui Liu, Ravi Prakash, Li-Yu Lo, Nils Roede, Boyuan Chen
papers.abstract: Aerial robots generate structured aeroacoustic fields during flight, yet these signals have been underexplored as a source of onboard relative perception, particularly under the strong ego-acoustic interference generated during simultaneous flight in various outdoor conditions. We introduce embodied passive aeroacoustic perception, a sensing paradigm in which an aerial robot infers actionable relative-state information from the naturally generated sound of flight while operating within its own evolving aeroacoustic field. We present SonicFly, a passive aeroacoustic perception framework that enables one unmanned aerial vehicle to estimate and follow another using only the leader's intrinsic flight sound, without active acoustic signaling, inter-robot communication, GPS sharing, or external sensing infrastructure. The system uses a lightweight four-microphone array, rotorcraft-informed acoustic representations, a neural bearing-range estimator, and confidence-gated filtering for closed-loop flight. Through acoustic characterization, onboard localization, and outdoor pursuit experiments, we show that multirotor aeroacoustic signals contain sufficient information to support relative perception despite strong ego-acoustic interference, environmental variability, and changing flight geometry. During acoustic-only pursuit, SonicFly achieved a mean distance-maintenance error of 1.34 m across diverse outdoor trajectories and operating conditions. Analysis of the acoustic channel reveals design principles governing embodied passive aeroacoustic perception, including the roles of harmonic structure, spectral separability, and spatial acoustic cues in determining observability. Our results establish the feasibility of embodied passive aeroacoustic perception for aerial robots and suggest that naturally generated behavioral signals can serve as information for robotic perception and coordination.
papers.summary_cn: 本文提出"具身被动气动声学感知"范式：无人机仅依靠自身飞行噪声即可推断相对位置并追踪伴机，无需通信、GPS或外部基础设施。SonicFly系统采用四麦克风阵列、声学特征提取与神经估计器，在强自噪声干扰下实现了平均1.34米的距离保持误差，为空中机器人协作提供了一种零额外载荷的感知方案。

strengths: Novel sensing paradigm exploiting naturally generated aeroacoustic fields for relative perception
End-to-end system with real outdoor pursuit experiments (1.34 m mean error)
Thorough acoustic channel analysis revealing design principles
limitations: Limited to pursuit scenario; generalization to other multi-robot tasks unclear
Strong ego-acoustic interference remains a challenge despite mitigation
Hardware-specific (four-microphone array); robustness to different platforms not tested
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Real outdoor experiments across diverse trajectories and conditions; acoustic characterization provides solid empirical foundation, though scale is limited to two-robot scenario
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Interesting and well-executed proof-of-concept with solid experimental validation, but niche application scope limits broader impact; novelty is genuine but incremental rather than groundbreaking

papers.title: Sovereign Cognitive Digital Twins: Fusing 6G ISAC, AI-RAN, and Zero-Trust Edge Grids for National Resilience in the Global South
papers.authors: Zoe Aiyanna M. Cayetano, George M. Gichuru, Taijuo T. Morris
papers.abstract: Small-island developing states face accelerating sea-level rise, intensifying cyclones, and storm surge, while suffering the sparse ground instrumentation that makes timely hazard perception difficult. This paper argues for a shift from passive cellular connectivity to the Network as a Sensor, realized through a Sovereign Cognitive Digital Twin (S-CDT): a federated national digital twin whose perceptual substrate is the 6G radio interface itself. Instead of disjoint sensing systems, a nation can reuse the Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) waveforms of its own network as a distributed radar mesh. We specify a six-layer S-CDT stack in which ISAC collapses the boundary between the dynamic-data and communication layers; we map the physical layer to the ETSI GR ISC 001 and 3GPP Release 19 sensing frameworks; and we formulate a belief-state control loop, an Extended Kalman Filter feeding a Proximal Policy Optimization agent, designed to absorb O-RAN telemetry delay. That loop is specified but not evaluated here. Beyond the reference architecture, we implement a reproducible, CPU-only geodata-to-ray-tracing pipeline over a 2 km study area at the Barbados Heritage District, Newton Plantation: 576 LiDAR-height buildings, a 70x70 terrain grid, and the government tower register become a Sionna RT scene. On identical geometry, median best-server path gain falls from -106 dB at 1.8 GHz to -122 dB at 10 GHz; concrete-only 28/60 GHz runs yield -130/-136 dB, with coverage contracting to line-of-sight lobes. These uncalibrated, 1x1 V-polarized simulations are framed as a towards-6G site model of the background channel, not an operational ISAC deployment. We treat data sovereignty and physical-layer zero-trust security as first-order design constraints. Barbados (166 km2, ~280k population) is the reference deployment, with the Philippines as an archipelagic generalization.
papers.summary_cn: 小岛屿发展中国家面临海平面上升、热带气旋和风暴潮加剧的威胁，却缺乏足够的地面监测设施。本文提出将6G无线接口本身作为感知 substrate，构建"主权认知数字孪生"（S-CDT）：利用ISAC波形作为分布式雷达网格，在巴巴多斯牛顿种植园遗产区开展2km²射线追踪仿真，验证了1.8GHz至60GHz的路径损耗模型，并将数据主权与物理层零信任安全作为首要设计约束。

strengths: Novel integration of ISAC, AI-RAN, and zero-trust for sovereign digital twins in developing states
Practical focus on Global South deployment challenges with real geodata pipeline
Well-specified six-layer architecture mapping to ETSI/3GPP frameworks
limitations: Control loop (EKF+PPO) specified but not evaluated—major gap
Ray-tracing results are uncalibrated 1x1 V-polarized simulations, not validated against measurements
Limited to 2 km study area; scalability to national deployment unclear
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Uses real LiDAR and terrain data for Barbados, but simulation-only evaluation without empirical validation of channel model or ISAC sensing performance
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Strong conceptual novelty and practical relevance for underserved regions, but incomplete technical validation reduces rigor score; impact potential is high if follow-up work delivers empirical results

papers.title: O-RAN: Analysis of Latency-critical Interfaces and Overview of Time Sensitive Networking Solutions
papers.authors: Esteban Municio, Gines Garcia-Aviles, Andres Garcia-Saavedra, Xavier Costa-Pérez
papers.abstract: 5G and B5G/6G foundations heavily rely on virtualization technologies, and virtualized Radio Access Networks (vRANs) are one of their major keystones. However, while vRANs have been traditionally suffering from significant hardware/software coupling, next generation vRANs aim for open, standardized interfaces and multi-vendor, interoperable components to enable truly flexible deployments following the cloud-native principles. In this line, the O-RAN Alliance is promoting a novel Open RAN architecture to further boost flexibility and cost efficiency. In order to reduce costs and effectively achieve the promised disaggregation levels, O-RAN must ensure shared, integrated transport networks in opposition to dedicated, over-provisioned links from traditional approaches. However, keeping deterministic performance requirements in such cost-effective networks (i.e., general-purpose Ethernet networks), especially in those interfaces that are time-critical, is a challenge. In this article, we review the most relevant Time Sensitive Networking (TSN) standards that may bring compelling benefits to O-RAN (i.e., IEEE 802.1CM, IEEE 802.1Qbu and IEEE 802.1Qbv) for providing determinism over cost-efficient networks. We explore the design space for a TSN-enabled O-RAN architecture, reporting on the requirements and deployment options and finally, we discuss on the opportunities and challenges that O-RAN will face when adopting TSN technologies to fully open the vRAN ecosystem.
papers.summary_cn: O-RAN联盟推动的开放架构需要共享传输网络来降低成本，但时间关键接口在通用以太网上保证确定性性能仍是挑战。本文综述了IEEE 802.1CM、Qbu、Qbv等TSN标准在O-RAN中的应用潜力，探讨了TSN使能的O-RAN架构设计空间、部署选项及面临的机遇与挑战，旨在通过时间敏感网络为虚拟化RAN提供确定性和开放性的兼容方案。

strengths: Comprehensive review of relevant TSN standards (IEEE 802.1CM, Qbu, Qbv) for O-RAN
Clear mapping of latency requirements to TSN capabilities
Practical discussion of deployment options and challenges
limitations: Purely review/survey paper with no new technical contributions
Lacks quantitative analysis or simulation of proposed TSN-O-RAN integration
Dated perspective (2021 era) may not reflect latest O-RAN developments
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: No original data; synthesizes existing standards documents and prior work; useful as reference but not a research contribution
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Useful survey for practitioners but limited research contribution; strong practical relevance for O-RAN deployment, but novelty is minimal as it primarily aggregates existing standards

papers.title: MAC-Gyver: Open, Programmable, Scheduling for AI-RAN 6G Systems
papers.authors: Maxime Elkael, Reshma Prasad, Tamerlan Aghayev, Salvatore D'Oro, Michele Polese, Tommaso Melodia
papers.abstract: Cellular networks are integrating Artificial Intelli- gence (AI) into radio access network control. The MAC scheduler is a promising target because it allocates a limited resource, spectrum, at every slot, under competing latency, throughput, and reliability requirements. However, most learning-based sched- ulers are evaluated only in simulation. Production schedulers are difficult to modify, and realistic stress tests require more radio hardware than most laboratories can provide. We present MAC-Gyver, an open-source framework for developing and evaluating scheduling applications that execute directly inside the OpenAirInterface scheduler. It exposes scheduler observations and controls through typed interfaces while preserving the underlying protocol and real-time execution paths. The same applications run over the air and in mac-emu, a PHY-less emulator that executes the unmodified OpenAirInterface Layer 2 stack for up to 90 users on one host at real-time slot pace, with a 3GPP-compliant channel model. To showcase the flexibility of MAC-Gyver, we evaluate two use cases. A proactive uplink scheduler predicts packet arrivals and roughly halves median round-trip latency. A frequency-selective uplink scheduler selects contiguous sub-bands from per-PRB sounding observations and is evaluated across mobility and power-limited operating points against an offline scheduling ceiling. Together, they show how the same production stack can be an AI playground that supports implementation, controlled evaluation, and over-the-air validation through complementary scheduling use cases.
papers.summary_cn: MAC-Gyver是一个开源框架，可直接在OpenAirInterface MAC调度器内开发AI调度应用，保留实时执行路径，支持空中测试与无物理层仿真器（mac-emu）。在90用户规模下验证了预测性上行调度将中位RTT延迟降低约一半，并展示了基于SRS的频选调度方案，证明同一生产代码栈可作为AI调度算法的开发、评估与验证平台。

strengths: Open-source framework enabling direct in-scheduler AI application development in production OAI stack
mac-emu emulator executes unmodified L2 stack at real-time pace for up to 90 users—strong validation tool
Two complementary use cases with measurable improvements (50% latency reduction, frequency-selective scheduling)
limitations: Evaluation limited to specific scenarios; broader applicability across different traffic patterns needs more exploration
OpenAirInterface-specific; portability to other RAN stacks not addressed
Hardware requirements for over-the-air testing may still be barrier for some labs
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Strong empirical evaluation with both emulation and over-the-air tests; realistic 3GPP-compliant channel model; reproducible open-source implementation
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Solid systems contribution with practical open-source tooling, rigorous evaluation, and clear path to adoption; fills real gap between simulation-only research and production deployment

papers.title: CSI-CLIP++: A Scalable Channel Foundation Model for Wireless Communication via CIR-CSI Consistency
papers.authors: Jun Jiang, Wenjun Yu, Yunfan Li, Yuan Gao, Shugong Xu
papers.abstract: Self-supervised learning can exploit large-scale unlabeled channel data to improve the transferability of wireless AI models. Existing channel foundation models are often built on single-domain representations or reconstruction-oriented objectives, which may not explicitly capture the physical correspondence between frequency- and delay-domain channel views. This paper proposes CSI-CLIP++, a scalable channel foundation model for MIMO wireless channels. CSI-CLIP++ treats frequency-domain channel state information (CSI) and delay-domain channel impulse response (CIR) as paired views of the same propagation process and learns transferable representations through CSI-CIR contrastive alignment. The pretrained CSI encoder is adapted to channel identification, beam prediction, and positioning, representing PHY, RAN, and ISAC applications. Experiments on large-scale DeepMIMO scenarios show consistent gains over supervised baselines across environments, carrier frequencies, and data scales. CSI-CLIP++ improves beam prediction Top-1 accuracy by up to 19.31 percentage points and achieves competitive positioning performance, including cross-simulator transfer on a Sionna RT dataset. Backbone scaling results further show that the proposed objective remains effective across encoder architectures and benefits from larger model capacity.
papers.summary_cn: CSI-CLIP++是一种可扩展的MIMO无线信道基础模型，将频域信道状态信息和时域信道冲激响应视为同一传播过程的配对视图，通过CSI-CIR对比对齐学习可迁移表示。预训练编码器可适配信道识别、波束预测和定位任务。在DeepMIMO场景中，波束预测Top-1精度提升最高19.31个百分点，并实现了跨仿真器迁移。

strengths: Novel CSI-CIR contrastive alignment explicitly captures physical correspondence between frequency and delay domains
Foundation model approach with self-supervised learning addresses key challenge of limited labeled channel data
Comprehensive evaluation across three distinct tasks: channel identification, beam prediction, and positioning
Cross-simulator transfer to Sionna RT dataset demonstrates strong generalization capability
Backbone scaling analysis shows architectural flexibility and path to improved performance
limitations: Contrastive learning requires paired CSI-CIR data which may not always be available in practice
Computational overhead of foundation model training may be prohibitive for some deployment scenarios
Real-world over-the-air validation not demonstrated; relies on ray-tracing simulations
Comparison with other recent wireless foundation models could be more extensive
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Large-scale DeepMIMO scenarios with cross-simulator transfer to Sionna; comprehensive synthetic but realistic data
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Strong novelty in physical-layer foundation model design with rigorous evaluation across multiple tasks and simulators

papers.title: Adaptive Machine Learning Framework for UAV Trajectory Optimization in O-RAN
papers.authors: Chenrui Sun, Swarna Bindu Chetty, Gianluca Fontanesi, Mahnaz Arvaneh, Walid Saad, Hamed Ahmadi
papers.affiliations: Radio Systems Research, Nokia Bell Labs, Stuttgart, Germany | School of Electrical and Electronic Engineering | Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Virginia Tech, VA | Recent research has also explored distributed artificial in
papers.abstract: The deployment of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) as open radio units (O-RUs) in 6G cellular systems presents a promising opportunity to achieve scalable and adaptive network coverage. However, optimizing UAV trajectories in dynamic and unfamiliar environments remains a critical challenge, particularly due to the need for extensive retraining in each new scenario. In this paper, we introduce a novel UAV trajectory optimization framework that integrates enhanced continual transfer learning within the O-RAN architecture. The proposed system maintains a library of pre-trained models and employs a model selection mechanism to identify and transfer knowledge from the most relevant environments, minimizing adaptation time and improving efficiency. When no sufficiently similar model is available, a fallback model empowered by continuous refinements ensures baseline performance. The framework leverages real-world city maps and ray tracing techniques to enhance learning reliability and improve trajectory planning. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed model selection-based transfer learning approach reduces convergence time by 44% to 56% compared to retraining from scratch, and up to 40% compared to traditional transfer learning without model selection.
papers.summary_cn: 将无人机（UAV）作为6G蜂窝系统中的开放无线单元（O-RU）部署，可实现可扩展和自适应的网络覆盖。本文提出一种集成增强持续迁移学习的UAV轨迹优化框架，在O-RAN架构下维护预训练模型库，通过模型选择机制从最相关环境迁移知识，相比从头训练减少44%至56%的收敛时间，相比传统迁移学习减少高达40%。

strengths: Novel continual transfer learning with model selection for UAV O-RU trajectory optimization
44-56% convergence time reduction vs. from-scratch is a strong and clearly quantified result
Up to 40% improvement over traditional transfer learning without model selection is meaningful
Real-world city maps and ray tracing enhance learning reliability — realistic environment modeling
Concrete fallback mechanism ensures robustness when no similar model exists
Well-integrated with O-RAN architecture; directly applicable to 6G UAV deployment
limitations: Fully simulation-based; no real UAV experiments or hardware validation
Ray tracing fidelity and city map representativeness not characterized
Model library growth and selection overhead at scale not discussed
8-10% improvement variance suggests training instability not fully addressed
No analysis of failure cases or when transfer learning actually hurts performance
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Simulation using real-world city maps and ray tracing; convergence time and energy metrics are well-defined; comparison baselines (from-scratch, traditional TL) are appropriate; scale of simulation scenarios unspecified.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Solid methodological contribution with clear quantitative gains and practical O-RAN integration. Simulation-only evaluation is the primary limitation, but the results are well-motivated and clearly presented with meaningful baselines.

papers.title: SkyChain Intelligence: A Blockchain-Secured Multi-Agent DRL Framework for Low-Altitude Embodied Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Haoxiang Luo, Tianqi Jiang, Ruichen Zhang, Yinqiu Liu, Gang Sun, Hongfang Yu, Abbas Jamalipour, Dong In Kim
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of the Low-Altitude Economy (LAE) ecosystem, Low-Altitude Embodied Artificial Intelligence (LAEAI) agents have become the core carriers of autonomous aerial services, thereby enabling dynamic Low-altitude Computility Networks (LACNets) for distributed computing resource sharing. However, resource-constrained LAEAI agents in decentralized LACNets face a fundamental trilemma of autonomy, security, and efficiency. Existing solutions primarily focus on either optimizing computational performance or enhancing security in isolation, failing to address the inherent trade-offs among trust, performance, and overhead in untrusted dynamic environments with malicious agents. To tackle this challenge, this paper proposes SkyChain Intelligence, a holistic framework that synergistically integrates agentic AI, consortium blockchain, and Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (MADRL). We design a lightweight blockchain-based decentralized trust management system with a dynamic reputation mechanism and develop a hybrid-action-space MADDPG algorithm that embeds on-chain reputation scores into the reward function to jointly optimize offloading decisions, resource allocation, and drone 3D trajectories. Extensive simulations demonstrate that our framework outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in task completion latency and energy consumption, while achieving a 94.1% task completion rate in the baseline scenario and stable convergence within 300 training episodes. This work provides a viable path for building secure, autonomous, and efficient machine-to-machine computing ecosystems in the low-altitude domain.
papers.summary_cn: 低空具身智能体是低空计算网络的核心，但面临自主性、安全与效率的三难困境。本文提出SkyChain Intelligence框架，融合智能体AI、联盟链与多智能体深度强化学习。设计轻量级去中心化信任管理系统，并开发混合动作空间算法联合优化卸载决策与轨迹。仿真显示，该框架在时延与能耗上优于现有方案，任务完成率达94.1%。

strengths: Addresses a genuine trilemma (autonomy, security, efficiency) in decentralized LACNets—problem framing is well-motivated
Integration of consortium blockchain with hybrid-action MADDPG is a reasonable approach to trust-aware resource management
Shows stable convergence within 300 episodes and 94.1% task completion rate in the baseline scenario
limitations: Entirely simulation-based; no real-world testing or even trace-driven evaluation with actual drone/network data
Blockchain overhead analysis (latency, gas cost, consensus delay) is largely absent—critical for resource-constrained LAEAI agents
The hybrid-action-space MADDPG is an incremental extension of existing MADDPG; core RL methodology is not novel
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Synthetic simulation only. No real datasets, no hardware experiments, no real-world workload traces. Blockchain performance metrics (throughput, transaction latency, consensus overhead) are not empirically evaluated.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: The trilemma framing is relevant, and the architecture design is reasonable, but the lack of real-world or even realistic trace-based evaluation, combined with absent blockchain overhead measurement, significantly weakens the contribution.

papers.title: LOLLA: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Closed-Loop Link Adaptation Towards a GPU-Accelerated AI-RAN
papers.authors: Rui Wang, Linchao Zhang, Qiang Liu, Kun Yang
papers.affiliations: Electronic Science and Technology of China, Quzhou | State Key Laboratory of Novel Software Technology | Engineering, Nanjing University (Suzhou Campus), Suzhou | University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, Chengdu
papers.abstract: Outer-loop link adaptation (OLLA) is widely deployed in 5G NR to track channel variations, yet its reliance on first-order, single-bit feedback degrades performance significantly under high-mobility and fast-varying channels. This paper presents LOLLA (Learned Outer-Loop Link Adaptation), a deep reinforcement learning framework that replaces the conventional OLLA staircase with a learned, continuous SINR offset conditioned on rich PHY/MAC telemetry inaccessible to OLLA. The offset modulates the SINR-to-MCS lookup table, preserving 3GPP-compliant MCS selection and provably subsuming the conventional OLLA update rule. A Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) policy trained under a Lagrangian block error rate (BLER) constraint automatically enforces tunable reliability targets from 1% to 15% without manual penalty calibration. The framework is realized as the first closed-loop AI-native control dApp on a GPU-accelerated 5G NR stack, achieving end-to-end control latencies under 500 microseconds. Evaluations under 3GPP TDL channel models demonstrate 15% to 92% throughput gains over OLLA across Doppler frequencies up to 400 Hz, while attaining a Pareto frontier that strictly dominates OLLA across all evaluated reliability targets. The learned policy generalizes to unseen channel models and scales to eight concurrent UEs under shared-resource scheduling. In the uplink formulation, the gNB directly observes decoding outcomes, enabling simulation-to-deployment parity.
papers.summary_cn: 传统外环链路自适应（OLLA）在5G NR中广泛部署，但其依赖一阶单比特反馈在高移动性和快变信道下性能显著下降。本文提出LOLLA框架，用深度强化学习替代传统OLLA阶梯式更新，基于丰富的PHY/MAC遥测数据学习连续SINR偏移量，保持3GPP兼容的MCS选择。该框架在GPU加速的5G NR协议栈上实现，端到端控制时延低于500微秒，在3GPP TDL信道模型下相比OLLA实现15%至92%的吞吐量增益，并在1%至15%可靠性目标范围内严格优于OLLA。

strengths: First closed-loop AI-native control dApp on GPU-accelerated 5G NR stack — novel system integration contribution
PPO policy with Lagrangian BLER constraint is principled; preserves 3GPP MCS selection compliance, enabling real deployment
15-92% throughput gains over OLLA across Doppler up to 400 Hz is a wide and impressive evaluation range
End-to-end control latency under 500 microseconds addresses a real and challenging engineering problem
Uplink formulation achieves sim-to-deployment parity — strong evidence of practical viability
Generalization to unseen channel models and scaling to 8 concurrent UEs demonstrates robustness
limitations: Evaluated only on 3GPP TDL channel models; no over-the-air or hardware-in-the-loop validation
GPU dependency for sub-500µs latency may limit deployment scope in low-cost RANs
BLER target range 1%-15% covers wide reliability but misses ultra-reliable URLLC regime (<0.1%)
Training complexity and hyperparameter sensitivity of PPO not discussed in detail
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: 3GPP TDL channel models (E, A, CDL) provide standardized and reproducible evaluation; 400 Hz Doppler covers high-mobility scenarios; no real-world over-the-air dataset; scale of 8 UEs is modest but reasonable for proof-of-concept.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Strong across all dimensions: novel system integration of DRL into 5G NR stack with provable compliance, impressive gains over baselines, sub-500µs latency is a genuine engineering achievement, and uplink parity demonstrates practical deployment readiness.

papers.title: High Speed High Signal-to-Noise Ratio Antenna Measurements -- Demonstration for UAV-Based Near-Field Measurements of Modulated Terrestrial Navigation Signals
papers.authors: Thomas F. Eibert, Denis Unruh, Thomas Mittereder, Alexander H. Paulus
papers.abstract: Antenna measurements with high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) require long measurement or integration times of the receiver and can, thus, lead to a very long duration of the measurements, especially if many frequency and spatial samples need to be collected. In order to speed up such measurements, an approach is presented, which collects all measurement samples with short measurement times, performs a Fourier transform of the measurement samples, bandpass filters the desired measurement signals with a small bandwidth, and obtains high-SNR measurement samples according to the short measurement times by inverse Fourier transform. This approach can be utilized with single-frequency continuous wave (CW) transmit signals, but also with transmit signals containing several discrete frequency components, as, e.g., found for periodically modulated CW carriers. The approach is first worked out and demonstrated for simulated test data. Next, it is utilized for the processing of modulated near-field (NF) measurement data collected via an uninhabited aerial vehicle (UAV) at a Doppler high-frequency omnidirectional radio range (DVOR) and at the localizer of an instrument landing system (ILS). The extracted CW NF data is transformed into the far field (FF) and diagnostic information is obtained from the underlying inverse source solutions.
papers.summary_cn: 为解决高信噪比天线测量耗时过长的问题，本文提出一种加速方法：采集短时测量样本，经傅里叶变换和带通滤波后，通过逆变换获得高信噪比数据。该方法适用于单频及调制连续波信号，并在DVOR和ILS的无人机近场测量数据中得到验证，成功提取诊断信息并转换至远场。

strengths: Methodologically sound approach to accelerating antenna measurements via FFT-bandpass-inverse FFT pipeline
Practical validation with real UAV-collected DVOR and ILS data (near-field to far-field transformation)
Addresses real-world measurement bottleneck of long integration times
Clear mathematical derivation and step-by-step signal processing chain
limitations: Peripheral relevance to AI-RAN/6G core topics; primarily an antenna/RF measurement paper
Limited algorithmic novelty — technique is an application of known Fourier-domain filtering principles
No discussion of applicability to 5G/6G communication signals beyond navigation signals (DVOR/ILS)
UAV platform specifics not deeply analyzed for generalizability
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Real UAV-based NF measurements for DVOR and ILS; simulations included for validation. Adequate for the antenna measurement focus but limited scale.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Solid antenna measurement contribution but low relevance to AI-RAN/6G network intelligence topics. Niche acceptance at antenna/RF venues but unlikely to be competitive at 6G/wireless communications conferences without stronger connection to communication system sensing.

overflow_list.title: Cross-Layer Optimization and System-Level Design of Next-Generation Wireless Networks via Intelligent RAN Control
overflow_list.authors: Maria Tsampazi
overflow_list.abstract: Recent years have seen the evolution of the traditional Radio Access Network (RAN) toward more open, programmable, disaggregated, and intelligent architectures, known as an Open RAN. Future Next Generation (NextG) networks are envisioned to be AI-native, enabling data-driven closed-loop optimization of Base Station resources, while Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) emerge as key enablers for wireless propagation and spectral efficiency toward 6G and beyond. This dissertation focuses on the design, optimization, and experimental evaluation of NextG RANs integrating Open RAN principles, data-driven control loops, and intelligent resource allocation. The work emphasizes cross-layer optimization, including energy-efficient power control, and explores AI-driven network slicing, scheduling, and link adaptation, demonstrating NextG RANs reconfigurable in real time to meet 6G requirements, first analyzing architectural enablers and modeling frameworks, then prototyping and evaluating solutions on experimental platforms and Digital Twins. Main contributions include: (i) Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) solutions for network slicing and scheduling; (ii) PandORA, a framework for automatic design, training, and deployment of DRL-based Open RAN applications on the Colosseum wireless network emulator; (iii) physical-layer RIS channel modeling and optimized resource allocation across spectrum bands; (iv) system-level evaluation of RIS-assisted channels for eMBB and URLLC traffic; (v) integration of RIS within Open RAN; (vi) online RL solutions for link adaptation; and (vii) spectrum sharing between cellular and Non-Terrestrial Network links via power control and beamforming. This work provides algorithmic designs, frameworks, and validation from simulation and hardware-in-the-loop emulation to over-the-air 5G testbed experiments, addressing industry and academic needs for wireless research.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 本文聚焦NextG RAN设计、优化与实验评估，集成Open RAN框架与AI原生控制。研究涵盖：DRL网络切片与调度方案；PandORA自动化DRL应用框架；RIS信道建模与资源优化；RIS辅助通信系统级评估；Open RAN中RIS集成；在线RL链路自适应；以及通过功率控制与波束成形实现星地频谱共享。从仿真、硬件在环仿真到5G现网实验全链路验证，为6G无线研究提供算法设计与框架支撑。

strengths: Comprehensive dissertation integrating Open RAN, DRL, RIS, and NTN into a unified NextG framework
PandORA framework for automatic DRL-based Open RAN application deployment on Colosseum is a well-designed systems contribution
Dual emphasis on algorithmic design and hardware-in-the-loop validation (simulation → emulation → over-the-air)
Covers end-to-end stack: from RIS physical-layer modeling to spectrum sharing with NTN
Link adaptation via online RL addresses a practical real-time challenge in reconfigurable RANs
limitations: Dissertation compilation nature: individual contributions are somewhat fragmented rather than deeply unified around one core insight
RIS integration within Open RAN (contribution v) lacks deep protocol-level or O-RAN interface specification detail
Simulation dominates; some claims (e.g., 'real-time reconfiguration to meet 6G requirements') are asserted without rigorous real-time latency bounds
NTN spectrum sharing contribution (vii) appears brief and less validated compared to core DRL and RIS sections
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Strong methodological diversity: simulation, Colosseum hardware-in-the-loop emulation, and over-the-air 5G testbed experiments. However, individual subsections show varying depth—some with extensive testbed validation, others with only simulation.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Well-engineered systems dissertation with credible validation pipeline; PandORA framework is a genuine systems contribution likely to be cited in O-RAN implementation work; RIS+Open RAN integration is forward-looking for 6G standardization.

overflow_list.title: LEO-Aware DRL Meta-Scheduler for 5G Non-Terrestrial Network Slicing
overflow_list.authors: Víctor Vilchez, Tiago P. C. de Andrade, Edward Hinojosa, Edmundo Madeira, and Carlos A. Astudillo
overflow_list.abstract: The integration of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs) into 5G and upcoming 6G architectures introduces various challenges, including severe propagation delays, ultra-high base station mobility, and channel non-stationarity, complicating radio resource management of heterogeneous network slices. In this paper, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) meta-scheduler for twin-timescale resource allocation. Our solution adopts a decoupled Open Radio Access Network (RAN) architecture, in which a strategic 100 ms meta-scheduler selects scheduling policies for the different network slices using stale telemetry, while a fast-timescale MAC packet scheduler processes per-TTI user requests. The resulting Markov Decision Process captures non-stationary orbital dynamics and heterogeneous SLAs constraints via a TD3 agent. Simulation results under varying traffic load show that, unlike other solutions, the proposed meta-scheduler explicitly trades a statistically insignificant 1% capacity fraction (p > 0.05) to strictly bound the variance and overall magnitude of RLC-layer queuing delay for Mission-Critical (MC) traffic. Crucially, it enforces this isolation without inducing the broadband slice starvation characteristic of standard maximum-CQI heuristics, establishing a robust foundation for 6G O-RAN NTN resource allocation.
overflow_list.summary_cn: LEO星地融合网络面临传播时延大、基站高速移动、信道非平稳等挑战。本文提出双时尺度DRL元调度器，采用解耦Open RAN架构：100ms战略级元调度器基于陈旧遥测为不同切片选配策略；快速MAC调度器按TTI处理用户请求。通过TD3智能体建模轨道非平稳动态与异构SLA约束。仿真表明，该方案仅牺牲1%容量（统计不显著），即实现任务关键业务队列时延的严格约束与方差控制，同时避免标准最大CQI策略导致的宽带切片饥饿问题。

strengths: Twin-timescale meta-scheduler architecture is a well-motivated and practical solution for O-RAN NTN integration
MDP formulation that explicitly captures LEO orbital dynamics and heterogeneous SLA constraints is methodologically sound
TD3 agent with rigorous statistical validation (p > 0.05) of capacity-delay tradeoff is a strength; the 1% capacity-for-stability tradeoff is clearly quantified
Demonstrates bounded queuing delay for MC traffic without inducing broadband slice starvation—a meaningful negative-result contribution
Addresses a real and timely problem: integrating high-mobility LEO NTNs into O-RAN resource management
limitations: Meta-scheduler at 100 ms timescale may be too slow for highly dynamic LEO handoffs in very low orbital altitudes (300-600 km)
Simulation-only evaluation; no hardware-in-the-loop or over-the-air validation
TD3 as choice is reasonable but not compared against other DRL algorithms (PPO, SAC) in sufficient depth
Stale telemetry handling is acknowledged but the staleness bounds and their sensitivity are not fully explored
Single satellite constellation assumption limits generalizability to multi-constellation scenarios
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Simulation results with varying traffic loads; statistically validated with p-values. Limited scenario diversity (single constellation, fixed traffic models), but the delay distribution and starvation analysis are thorough within those bounds.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Technically grounded paper addressing a real 6G O-RAN NTN challenge; the statistical rigor of the capacity-delay tradeoff and starvation avoidance results are likely to influence O-RAN NTN resource allocation discussions. Strong conference/journal submission potential.

overflow_list.title: Degeneracy-Aware Resource Allocation for Resilient 6G RAN
overflow_list.authors: Sayanti Ghosh, Indrakshi Dey, Nicola Marchetti
overflow_list.abstract: Heterogeneous 6G radio access networks (RANs) must allocate resources reliably under interference, latency limits, imperfect channel state information (CSI), and architectural diversity. We propose a degeneracy-aware resource allocation (DG-RA) framework that casts multi-architecture orchestration as a probabilistic game and, unlike single-solution optimization, deliberately favors allocations realizable by many structurally distinct yet performance-equivalent strategy profiles. Resilience is quantified across three layers through Degeneracy-Weighted Path Robustness (DWPR), Functional Substitution Score (FSS), and an Algorithmic Resilience Quotient (ARQ). Across centralized (C-RAN), open (O-RAN), virtualized (V-RAN), and hybrid RAN architectures, and benchmarked against a fractional-programming optimizer, DG-RA matches the state-of-the-art throughput and outage at the static operating point, then exploits its equivalence set to recover $\sim$$99\%$ of throughput from a resource-unit failure with a single switch, where a single-solution optimizer needs tens of iterations to re-converge. The results recast degeneracy not as a rate booster but as a precomputed resilience reserve for disruption-tolerant 6G orchestration.
overflow_list.summary_cn: DG-RA：6G异构RAN的退化感知资源分配框架。将多架构编排建模为概率博弈，引入DWPR、FSS、ARQ三层韧性指标。在C-RAN/O-RAN/V-RAN/混合架构中，静态性能持平最优方案；遭遇资源单元故障时，单次切换即可恢复约99%吞吐量（传统优化器需数十次迭代）。将"退化"从速率助推器重构为抗扰动的韧性储备。

strengths: Highly original framing: degeneracy (multiple performance-equivalent solutions) as a resilience reserve rather than a performance booster
Three-layer resilience quantification (DWPR, FSS, ARQ) provides principled multi-dimensional evaluation
Cross-architecture validation across C-RAN, O-RAN, V-RAN, and hybrid — rare breadth
Single-switch recovery of ~99% throughput after resource failure, dramatically faster than iterative re-convergence
Probabilistic game formulation is theoretically grounded
limitations: Simulation-only evaluation; no hardware testbed or real-world deployment data
Degeneracy quantification may be computationally expensive for large action spaces
Fractional-programming baseline comparison may not represent the strongest alternative (e.g., no comparison to robust optimization)
Theoretical assumptions about knowledge of equivalence sets may not hold in practice
Limited ablation: impact of each resilience layer (DWPR/FSS/ARQ) not isolated
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Simulation-based evaluation across four RAN architectures; no real hardware or operational data. Baselines include fractional-programming optimizer and single-solution approaches.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Novel and compelling idea — reframing degeneracy as resilience reserve is conceptually significant. Strong practical impact for 6G orchestration. Moderate deduction for simulation-only data and some clarity gaps in the three-metric framework presentation. Solid theoretical contribution with good architectural breadth.

overflow_list.title: VeraRAN: Pre-Actuation Certification and Event-Causal Synchronization Repair for Asynchronous Multi-Interface RAN Plans
overflow_list.authors: Yinghan Hou, Zongyou Yang
overflow_list.abstract: Agentic RAN controllers combine mobility, energy, and resource actions across independently implemented interfaces. Even when each command is valid and the target state is safe, asynchronous actuation can drive the network through unsafe intermediate states. In a frozen study of a 35B planner, 28.8% of locally valid plans remained asynchronously unsafe. We introduce VeraRAN, which checks plans before actuation by modeling request, delivery, acceptance, application, completion, and observation for each action while exploring plausible delays and event orders. When VeraRAN finds a counterexample, VeraSync inserts versioned event barriers and rechecks the repaired plan for safety and completion. MI-POR prunes independent interleavings using RAN lifecycle and resource footprints. In a post-freeze stratified confirmation within the declared repair domain, VeraSync re-certified every confirmation plan while leaving 87% of action pairs unordered. MI-POR matched exact search in a property-stratified audit and reduced explored states by 94.6-95.0% on 20-40-action plans. Native ns-O-RAN replay and an independent live E2 audit showed why distinguishing these events matters: acceptance may precede the authoritative state transition, so dependent actions must wait for direct APPLY evidence or a contract-backed completion event causally downstream of APPLY.
overflow_list.summary_cn: VeraRAN：解决O-RAN agent控制器异步执行导致中间态不安全的问题。28.8%的局部有效计划存在异步风险。VeraRAN建模请求-交付-接受-应用-完成-观察六阶段并穷举时序；发现反例后通过VeraSync插入版本化事件屏障重新验证；MI-POR基于生命周期和资源足印剪枝独立交错。实测减少94.6-95.0%状态探索，同时保留87%动作对为无序。

strengths: Identifies a critical but underexplored problem: async unsafe intermediate states in agentic RAN controllers
VeraSync (versioned event barriers) + MI-POR (state pruning) form a practical two-stage solution
94.6-95.0% state space reduction via MI-POR while matching exact search — impressive scalability
Native ns-O-RAN replay + live E2 audit with real-world event ordering nuance (acceptance preceding state transition)
28.8% of valid plans found unsafe in frozen study quantifies the severity of the problem
limitations: Frozen study on 35B planner; unclear if findings generalize to other planners/scales
VeraSync repair approach (inserting event barriers) may add latency overhead — not quantified
ns-O-RAN replay is simulation; real-world deployment challenges not explored
MI-POR pruning strategy not fully detailed; reproducibility concerns
87% action pairs left unordered may still contain hidden dependencies in complex scenarios
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Frozen study on a 35B planner (model unspecified), ns-O-RAN simulation replay, and independent live E2 audit. No large-scale dataset; validation is experimental and multi-method but not comprehensive.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: High novelty — the async safety problem in agentic RAN controllers is underexplored and practically important. VeraSync + MI-POR solution is architecturally sound with strong state-reduction results. Confidence medium because key details (planner model, barrier overhead) are missing. Impact is very high if the problem is as prevalent as the 28.8% finding suggests.

overflow_list.title: METIS: A Declarative Slice Orchestrator for Application-Centric 5G/6G Networks
overflow_list.authors: Arman Divband, Ali Yaghoubian, Navid Nikaein
overflow_list.abstract: Network slicing is the cornerstone of application-aware 5G and 6G networks, yet dynamic lifecycle management of network slice instances with coordinated quality-of-service enforcement across the radio access network and core network remains unresolved. Existing orchestrators rely on network-centric data models, imperative workflows, and static slice templates, while O-RAN addresses radio-side slice control independently of 3GPP core-side control, leaving slice-level quality-of-service enforcement uncoordinated across domains. This paper introduces METIS, a declarative slice orchestrator that manages the Day-0/1/2 lifecycle of network slice instances through cascaded reconciliation loops. METIS defines an application-centric data model for service profiles, enabling customers to describe the semantics and quality-of-experience requirements of their applications. From these, METIS derives 3GPP-aligned slice profiles via hierarchical aggregation following the 5G quality-of-service model, eliminating static templates, and jointly coordinates O-RAN and 3GPP slicing for slice instantiation and enforcement. Our central finding is a structural asymmetry in end-to-end slice control: downlink traffic can be shaped at the core before reaching the radio access network, but uplink leaves the user equipment unregulated, so core-only slicing cannot reliably satisfy uplink service-level agreements - radio-side enforcement is necessary, not merely complementary. Evaluated on a 5G cloud-native testbed in a campus-event scenario, METIS completes slice creation, update, upgrade, and deletion within 22.4, 5.1, 52.2, and 32.1 seconds, respectively; sustains full service-level-agreement satisfaction under concurrent multi-slice overload; scales to 63 slice instances across nine zones consuming under 0.03 processor cores total; and recovers slices from injected failures across four levels in under 19 seconds.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 本文提出 METIS，一种声明式网络切片编排器，通过级联调谐循环管理切片全生命周期。METIS 以应用为中心的数据模型使客户可描述语义和体验质量需求，并推导出 3GPP 对齐的切片配置文件，协调 O-RAN 与 3GPP 切片控制。核心发现：端到端切片控制存在结构性不对称——下行可在核心侧整形，但上行走用户设备未受监管，核心侧切片无法可靠满足上行 SLA，无线侧强制执行不可或缺。测试表明创建、更新、升级、删除分别在 22.4、5.1、52.2、32.1 秒内完成。

strengths: Real 5G cloud-native testbed evaluation—strongest empirical grounding in the set
Declarative model eliminates static templates; addresses real operational friction
Structural asymmetry finding (uplink vs. downlink) is a genuinely novel and actionable insight
Joint O-RAN + 3GPP coordination is architecturally important and well-executed
Performance numbers are specific and credible: 22.4s slice creation, 63 slices on 0.03 CPU cores
Scalability and failure recovery demonstrated convincingly
limitations: Campus-event scenario may not represent high-mobility or ultra-reliable use cases
Application-centric data model abstraction may lose fine-grained QoS control needed by some verticals
Slice deletion time (32.1s) is relatively high compared to creation
No comparison against commercial orchestrators (e.g., OSM, ONAP)
METIS architecture assumes O-RAN and 3GPP alignment that may not exist in legacy deployments
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Evaluated on real 5G cloud-native testbed. Specific latency/throughput metrics reported. Multi-slice overload and four-level failure injection experiments provide robustness validation. Strong data quality for a systems paper.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Top paper in this set. High novelty (declarative orchestration, uplink asymmetry finding), strong rigor (real testbed), excellent data quality, and very high practical impact. Closest to deployable of all submissions.

overflow_list.title: When 5G MIMO Scaling Breaks: Toward 6G Upper-Mid-Band Extreme MIMO
overflow_list.authors: Kwang Soon Kim, Jeonghun Park, Byung-Wook Min, Kwanghoon Lee, Eui Whan Jin, Juntaek Han, Geonwoo Park, Jun-Seok Ko, Jungho Myung, Wooram Shin, Young-Jo Ko, Chan-Byoung Chae
overflow_list.abstract: The upper-mid band, particularly the 7-8 GHz range within frequency range 3 (FR3), has emerged as a leading spectrum candidate for wide-area sixth-generation (6G) cellular networks. Its shorter wavelength enables hundreds of antenna elements to be integrated within the physical aperture of an existing 5G base-station panel. In principle, the resulting aperture gain can compensate for the increased path loss and enable extreme MIMO (E-MIMO) with 256 or more antenna ports while reusing current cell sites. In practice, however, simply scaling the 5G New Radio (NR) architecture from tens to hundreds of ports encounters fundamental system-level limitations. This paper identifies where 5G-style MIMO scaling breaks and develops a research roadmap for practical upper-mid-band E-MIMO. We first review the evolution of FR3 spectrum, its propagation and channel characteristics, and the emerging 6G system requirements. We then organize the principal challenges into four coupled areas: maintaining effective coverage across all physical channels and protocol states; implementing wideband, energy-efficient RF devices and radio units; developing new low-power array and beamforming architectures; and acquiring sufficiently refined channel state information with manageable sounding and feedback overhead. Representative system studies illustrate the coverage asymmetry between user-specific data transmission and common or channel-acquisition signals, as well as the spectral- and energy-efficiency tradeoffs among fully digital, hybrid, tri-hybrid, dynamic-metasurface, and fluid-antenna architectures. Finally, we discuss how distributed apertures, integrated sensing, AI-assisted channel acquisition, and environment-aware operation can transform fixed-aperture scaling into a deployable 6G E-MIMO architecture.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 7-8 GHz上中频频段（FR3）已成为6G广域蜂窝网络的主要候选频谱。其较短波长可在现有5G基站面板物理孔径内集成数百个天线单元，实现256端口以上的极端MIMO（E-MIMO）。本文识别5G MIMO架构从数十端口扩展到数百端口时遇到的系统级瓶颈，从覆盖有效性、射频器件、阵列架构和信道状态信息获取四个方面提出研究路线图。

strengths: Identifies a critical and underappreciated problem: where 5G NR MIMO scaling fundamentally breaks at 100+ ports in the FR3 7-8 GHz band
Comprehensive four-area challenge taxonomy (coverage, RF hardware, array architecture, CSI acquisition) provides a structured research roadmap rather than a point solution
Coverage asymmetry analysis between data transmission and common/channel-acquisition signals is a key insight not addressed in prior literature
Architecture tradeoff study (fully digital, hybrid, tri-hybrid, dynamic-metasurface, fluid-antenna) with spectral and energy efficiency metrics is rigorous and comparative
Considers practical deployment by reusing existing cell sites, which directly addresses operator concerns
AI-assisted channel acquisition and environment-aware operation directions are forward-looking and well-motivated
The research roadmap structure makes this highly actionable for both academia and industry
limitations: No hardware validation of the proposed architectures — simulation and analytical tradeoffs are compelling but unvalidated at scale
Channel models for FR3 7-8 GHz, while referenced, may not reflect real-world propagation complexity (e.g., building materials, atmospheric effects at higher frequencies)
Cost and complexity tradeoffs of the advanced antenna architectures (tri-hybrid, fluid-antenna) are mentioned but not rigorously quantified
AI-assisted channel acquisition section is more of a vision than a concrete methodology — lacks algorithm design or simulation results
Distributed aperture discussion is brief and lacks quantitative system-level analysis
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: System studies based on simulations with realistic propagation assumptions for FR3. Architecture comparisons use consistent metric definitions across schemes. No large-scale real deployment dataset, but channel characterization draws on established measurement campaigns and standard 3GPP models. Among the papers reviewed, this has the strongest analytical and comparative evidence base.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Highest-impact paper in this set. The problem framing ('where 5G MIMO scaling breaks') is a genuine contribution to 6G spectrum strategy discussions. Rigorous system-level analysis with practical architectural comparisons. Likely to be cited as a foundational reference for upper-mid-band E-MIMO research. Strong acceptance at top venues (IEEE ComMag, TWC level). Minor deductions for lack of hardware validation and the somewhat premature AI-channel-acquisition discussion.

overflow_list.title: Artificial Intelligence for Spatially Reconfigurable Antennas: Movable, Fluid, and Pinching Antenna Systems
overflow_list.authors: Nguyen Cong Luong, Zeping Sui, Thai-Hoc Vu, Jie Cao, Bo Ma, Thuan Van Le, Xunyang Zhan, Nguyen Duc Hai, Min Xu, Qiushi Zhao, Dong In Kim, Yonghong Zeng, Shaohan Feng
overflow_list.abstract: Recently, sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks have moved beyond fixed-array designs toward antenna architectures that can adapt their spatial configuration to specific environmental conditions. Movable antenna, fluid antenna, and pinching antenna systems represent this principle in different ways, but they share a common vision: exploiting spatial flexibility as an additional degree of freedom (DoF) to improve communication, sensing, security, and resource efficiency. These new techniques, however, also bring challenging problems, as antenna configuration must be jointly considered with channel acquisition, beamforming, mobility, and network resource management. Therefore, artificial intelligence (AI) has become an important tool for learning fast and adaptive control policies for these highly coupled systems. In this survey, we provide a unified review of AI for spatially reconfigurable antenna systems. We first introduce the basic principles of movable, fluid, and pinching antennas, which is followed by a summary of the latest AI-enabled designs according to their primary optimization objectives. Furthermore, we compare the roles of deep learning (DL), deep reinforcement learning (DRL), multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), graph learning, Transformers, large language models (LLMs), and structure-guided learning across different antenna architectures. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future directions toward scalable, robust, and hardware-aware intelligent reconfigurable antenna networks.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 6G天线系统正从固定阵列向可空间重构演进。可移动天线、流体天线及机械针刺天线各具特色，共同将空间灵活性作为新的自由度提升通信、感知、安全与资源效率。本文综述AI赋能的空间可重构天线系统：介绍基本原理，按优化目标梳理最新AI设计方案；对比深度学习、DRL、多智能体RL、图学习、Transformer、大语言模型及结构引导学习在各类天线架构中的作用；并讨论面向可扩展、鲁棒、硬件感知智能重构天线网络的开放挑战与未来方向。

strengths: Unified survey covering three distinct reconfigurable antenna paradigms (movable, fluid, pinching) under AI enables cross-domain comparison
Comprehensive AI technique taxonomy: DL, DRL, MARL, graph learning, Transformers, LLMs, and structure-guided learning
Organized by optimization objectives (communications, sensing, security, resource efficiency) which provides a useful problem-driven structure
Excellent breadth—covers the full stack from antenna physics to network resource management
Timely survey as these antenna technologies are emerging and no comprehensive AI-focused review existed
limitations: Survey nature: no original experimental or theoretical contributions; depth varies significantly across topics
Hardware-aware discussion is superficial—many papers cited are simulation-only, and real hardware implementation challenges are not critically analyzed
Lumped comparison of fundamentally different AI techniques across architectures without a unifying benchmark makes comparative assessment difficult
Missing: systematic comparison table of AI technique suitability for each antenna type and objective
Forward-looking claims (scalable, robust, hardware-aware intelligent networks) are aspirational without concrete validation pathways
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Literature survey without new data; references existing works. Coverage is broad but depth per topic is limited. No quantitative comparison framework or benchmark across the surveyed approaches.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Strong survey for a premier venue (IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials target); high citation potential as the field matures. The unification of three reconfigurable antenna paradigms under AI is the paper's key value. Will serve as a reference for researchers entering this emerging area.

overflow_list.title: Powering Net-Zero 6G: Packetized Energy Management for Grid-Interactive Telecom Infrastructure
overflow_list.authors: Adnan Aijaz, Xinyi Lin
overflow_list.abstract: The transition to net-zero 6G requires energy-management approaches that go beyond conventional RAN efficiency mechanisms. As future networks integrate AI-native operation, edge intelligence, dense deployments, renewables, and storage, the RAN will become both a growing power consumer and a source of distributed energy flexibility. This paper introduces packetized energy management (PEM) as a framework for transforming 6G infrastructure into energy-aware, grid-interactive assets. PEM represents flexible demand as schedulable energy packets that can be admitted, deferred, or reshaped according to local constraints, renewable availability, carbon intensity, price, and communication priorities. We present a PEM-enabled base-station model, a RAN architecture for PEM integration, and the telecoms virtual power plant (VPP) concept for aggregating PEM-enabled sites. Simulation results demonstrate PEM's potential for peak-aware operation, improved renewable utilization, and outage-resilient service continuity. The paper also discusses open challenges for telco-energy co-design.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 6G净零转型需要超越传统RAN效率的能源管理方案。本文提出包化能源管理（PEM）框架，将6G基础设施转变为能源感知、可与电网交互的资产。PEM将灵活需求表示为可调度能源包，根据本地约束、可再生能源可用性、碳强度、价格和通信优先级进行接纳、延迟或整形。仿真结果证明PEM可实现峰谷感知运行、改善可再生能源利用和 outage-resilient服务连续性。

strengths: Packetized energy management (PEM) is a genuinely novel framing that translates energy flexibility into schedulable packets — bridges telecom and power-system communities
The telecom VPP concept for aggregating PEM-enabled sites is well-motivated and directly applicable to grid-interactive RAN
Peak-aware operation, renewable integration, and outage resilience are all practically important for net-zero 6G targets
PEM-enabled base-station model and RAN architecture are concrete enough to enable future work
Addresses a critically underserved topic — 6G energy sustainability beyond RAN efficiency metrics
Clear positioning relative to conventional RAN energy-saving approaches (sleep modes, DTX)
Simulation results cover multiple scenarios (peak shaving, renewable utilization, outage resilience)
limitations: PEM formulation assumes predictable energy flexibility — real-world traffic patterns and bursty services may violate this assumption
No discussion of the coordination overhead or signaling required to implement PEM across a distributed RAN
Grid modeling appears simplified; carbon intensity variations and real-time pricing dynamics are not deeply integrated
Security and privacy implications of grid-interactive telecom (exposing RAN schedules to grid operators) are not addressed
Simulation results are evaluated in isolation; no co-simulation with actual power grid models (e.g., IEEE grid test cases)
Business model and regulatory barriers to telecom VPP participation are mentioned but not analyzed
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Simulation-based validation with synthetic load profiles, renewable availability traces, and carbon intensity models. No real grid data or deployed telecom site measurements. Renewable and carbon data appear to be from publicly available datasets but are not explicitly cited. Results demonstrate concept viability rather than deployment readiness.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Highly novel concept with strong practical motivation for net-zero 6G. The telecom VPP framing is likely to attract attention from both telecom and energy systems researchers. Expected to be well-received at the intersection of communications and smart grid communities. Deductions for the gap between the compelling conceptual framework and rigorous grid co-simulation validation. Would be strengthened significantly by integration with established power system test cases.

overflow_list.title: Coexistence of 5G NR and Wi Fi 6E/7 at 6 GHz: Experimental Interference Measurements
overflow_list.authors: Rafik Zitouni, Demos Serghiou, Ali Dagdeviren, Tajinder Randhawa, Edwards Udean, Hanli Dong, Riccardo Pozza, Rahim Tafazolli
overflow_list.abstract: This paper presents the first conducted-interference measurements of a commercial Very Low Power (VLP) Wi-Fi 6E/7 device into both the gNB uplink and UE downlink receiver chains of a live 5G New Radio (NR) system, using a complete O-RAN/SDR stack with 5G core in band~n102 (6\,GHz). We use a Software-Defined Radio (SDR) testbed built on OpenAirInterface with band~n102 support (40 MHz, 30 kHz Subcarrier Spacing). We sweep the injected Wi-Fi power and record throughput, block error rate, and signal-to-noise ratio on both the gNB uplink and UE downlink paths. Neither receiver shows measurable degradation below 75 dBm. Above this threshold, performance degrades progressively. The UE is more resilient at lower data rates and unaffected by beacon-only transmissions. A complementary link-budget analysis maps these measured thresholds to equivalent VLP-to-victim distances. These distances fall well inside the 545--685 Listen Before Talk (LBT) exclusion zone, confirming that a compliant VLP device would vacate the channel before its emissions could harm either receiver.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 本文首次对商用超低功率（VLP）Wi-Fi 6E/7设备对现网5G NR的上行gNB和下行UE接收链路的传导干扰进行了实测。采用OpenAirInterface SDR测试平台，5G频段n102（6 GHz），40 MHz带宽，30 kHz子载波间隔。实验系统包括完整的O-RAN/SDR架构和5G核心网。通过扫描注入Wi-Fi功率，测量上下行吞吐量、误块率及信噪比。结果显示：低于−75 dBm时两链路均无明显性能下降；超出该阈值后性能逐步恶化；UE在低数据率下更为稳健，且不受仅信标传输影响。辅以链路预算分析，将实测阈值映射为等效VLP设备与受害接收机的距离。该距离远小于LBT exclusion zone的545–685米，因此符合LBT协议的VLP设备将在干扰达到有害电平前释放信道。

strengths: First conducted-interference measurements of commercial VLP Wi-Fi 6E/7 into live 5G NR system with complete O-RAN/SDR stack
Uses OpenAirInterface with real O-RAN fronthaul and 5G core—high-fidelity lab experiment with proper measurement methodology
-75 dBm interference threshold clearly established with progressive degradation above it
Link-budget mapping of thresholds to VLP-to-victim distances provides directly actionable guidance for coexistence standards
Confirmation that compliant LBT exclusion zones (545-685 m) are sufficient is a significant practical finding for regulators
limitations: Single 40 MHz channel (band n102) measurement; limited generalization to other 5G NR channel bandwidths or carrier frequencies
Only one specific VLP device and one gNB/UE device pair tested; device-specific effects may dominate results
No field measurements or real-world coexistence scenarios; pure lab conducted measurements
UE resilience at lower data rates is qualitatively described without systematic data
Missing: multi-cell scenarios, outdoor-to-indoor propagation effects, and concurrent multiple VLP devices
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Controlled lab experiment with systematic power sweeps; measures throughput, BLER, and SNR on both uplink and downlink paths. Sample sizes and repeatability are not fully documented, and the scenario space is narrow (single device pair, single channel).
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Strong experimental contribution with high practical impact for coexistence standardization; the -75 dBm threshold finding and LBT exclusion zone validation are directly relevant to 3GPP and regulatory discussions. Well-suited for IEEE Wireless Communications or similar applications-oriented venues.

overflow_list.title: Secure Relay Low-Altitude Networks via Hybrid Fixed-Position and Rotatable Antenna Arrays
overflow_list.authors: Maolin Li, Qi Zhang, Riqing Chen, Wei Gao, Feng Shu, Liang Yang, Cunhua Pan
overflow_list.abstract: In this paper, a relay network with hybrid fixed-position and rotatable antenna arrays is proposed. The deployment of rotatable arrays in conventional relay networks is considered to provide more secure communications for low-altitude economy applications. Specifically, both the base station and the relay station are equipped with fixed-position antenna arrays and rotatable arrays to serve ground users and aerial users, respectively. To address the challenge of multi-user interference, a low-cost reconfigurable intelligent surface is exploited as a candidate path. Accordingly, under constraints on transmit power, user quality of service, rotatable range, and path selection, the objective is to maximize the worst-case secrecy rate (SR) through joint beamforming, power allocation, and rotatable antenna orientation design. First, the SR performance in the single-user scenario is investigated, and a step-by-step leakage-based scheme is proposed. Then, the general multi-user scenario is studied, and a Distributional Soft Actor-Critic with Three refinements (DSAC-T)-based learning scheme, which supports hybrid discrete and continuous actions, is proposed to maximize the worst-case SR. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed schemes. The proposed schemes achieve approximately a twofold improvement in SR performance compared to isotropic antennas. The proposed system achieves approximately 71.4\% power saving, 55\% antenna saving, and can serve more users.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 本文提出混合固定与可旋转天线阵列的中继网络，为低空经济应用提供安全通信。基站和中继站均配备固定阵子和可旋转阵列分别服务地面和空中用户。采用可重构智能表面辅助多用户干扰抑制，在发射功率、用户 QoS、旋转范围、路径选择约束下，通过联合波束赋形、功率分配和天线方向设计最大化最差保密速率。单用户场景提出逐级泄漏方案，多用户场景提出 DSAC-T 学习方案。仿真显示相比各向同性天线保密速率提升约一倍，功耗节省约 71.4%，天线节省约 55%。

strengths: Hybrid fixed + rotatable antenna architecture is genuinely novel for low-altitude relay security
DSAC-T with hybrid discrete/continuous actions addresses realistic actuator constraints
RIS as fallback path is practical and cost-effective design choice
Worst-case secrecy rate maximisation is appropriate for security-critical applications
~2x SR improvement and 71.4% power saving / 55% antenna saving are compelling quantitative gains
limitations: RIS integration assumed ideal phase shift—practical RIS non-idealities not addressed
Rotatable antenna orientation assumes mechanical control feasibility in UAV context (weight, power, latency)
Single-tier threat model (eavesdropper only); jamming or full-spectrum attacks not considered
Low-altitude assumption limits generalisability to high-altitude platforms
DSAC-T learning scheme not compared against other actor-critic baselines
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Simulation-based evaluation with numerical results. Power/antenna savings reported; no real over-the-air experiments. RIS modelling appears standard. Moderate data quality for a theoretical paper.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Strong technical contribution in physical-layer security for low-altitude economy. Novel hybrid antenna architecture with practical relevance. DSAC-T approach is sound though not compared to state-of-the-art RL. Good balance of optimization theory and learning-based methods.

overflow_list.title: Can We Trust AI in 6G? Verifiable and Auditable AI-Driven Trustworthy Wireless Networks
overflow_list.authors: Genze Jiang, Yizhou Huang, Kezhi Wang
overflow_list.abstract: Mobile network operators are increasingly exploring the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to automate complex network tasks, such as cell selection and mobility management. A fundamental problem arises: there is currently no way to verify that an AI function is making the right decisions or for the right reasons, rather than arriving at correct-looking answers through unreliable shortcuts. In safety-critical and resilience-focused infrastructure, this lack of transparency poses a significant challenge to the widespread adoption of AI technologies in wireless networks. In this paper, we propose a mechanical auditing approach: inspecting a function's internal representations and checking them against machine-verifiable 3GPP specifications. Specifically, we set out a general three-step auditing principle that locates protocol-relevant features, verifies their causal role, and diagnoses how adaptation reshapes their use, grounding it throughout publicly available interpretability and telecommunications research. We present an audit-native network architecture in which a dedicated verification agent continuously checks the reasoning of AI functions in networks, supporting both predeployment certification and runtime auditing. We also discuss how it could be realised, the data and benchmarks, as well as the open challenges that remain before mechanistic auditing can enter telecommunications practice and standardisation.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 移动网络运营商正探索用AI自动化网络任务，但无法验证AI决策是否正确或出于正确原因，存在可靠性隐患。本文提出机械审计方法：检查AI函数内部表征并对照机器可验证的3GPP规范进行校验。设计了审计原生网络架构，由专用验证代理持续检查AI推理过程，支持部署前认证和运行时审计。

strengths: The core problem — verifying that AI in wireless networks is right for the right reasons, not lucky shortcuts — is critically important and largely unaddressed in the literature
Three-step auditing principle (locate protocol-relevant features, verify causal role, diagnose adaptation effects) is a principled and general framework
Grounding AI interpretability methods in concrete 3GPP specifications is a novel cross-disciplinary contribution
Audit-native network architecture with a dedicated verification agent is a concrete, deployable design
Addresses both pre-deployment certification and runtime auditing — covers the full AI lifecycle
Very timely given regulatory pressure (EU AI Act, network resilience requirements) for AI in critical infrastructure
Interpretability + telecom convergence is an emerging research direction this paper could anchor
limitations: Mechanistic interpretability tools (used in Step 1) are not yet mature enough for the complexity of production wireless stacks — maturity gap not adequately addressed
The 3GPP specification grounding relies on existing specs; as AI-native 6G features are defined (Rel-20+), the specification corpus will need continuous updating — this dynamic is not addressed
Runtime verification overhead (computational, latency) of the verification agent in a live RAN is not characterized
No empirical evaluation of the auditing approach on actual AI models (e.g., trained cell-selection or mobility-management policies)
The verification agent itself is an AI system — who audits the auditor? Circular trust problem not resolved
Benchmark datasets and standardized evaluation metrics for AI-in-wireless auditing are identified as open but not provided — limits reproducibility
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Conceptual and architectural contribution without empirical benchmarking. No evaluation against real AI models, no dataset for telecom-specific interpretability benchmarks, no runtime overhead measurements. Reliance on publicly available interpretability research (from CV/NLP domains) adapted to the wireless context. Findings are well-argued but the paper is primarily a position/framework paper awaiting empirical validation.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Potentially the most influential paper in this set for the trustworthy AI-in-wireless direction. The problem framing is novel and addresses a genuine gap in AI adoption for critical networks. Likely to be highly cited and serve as a reference for future work on AI verification in telecommunications. Deductions for the current absence of empirical validation and the maturity gap of interpretability tools applied to wireless AI. Expected strong acceptance at top venues (IEEE S&P, TMC, ComMag) given the timeliness and originality of the problem framing.

overflow_list.title: C-RE-ACT: Causal RE-ACTing Agent for O-RAN Forensic Triage
overflow_list.authors: Pau Baguer, J. Xavier Salvat Lozano, Gines Garcia-Aviles, Xavier Costa-Pérez
overflow_list.abstract: The shift to O-RAN architectures marks a turning point in cellular security, where increased openness and modularity directly translate into a broader attack surface. Among the security threats cataloged by the O-RAN Alliance Working Group 11, performance-degradation attacks constitute the largest class. These attacks induce packet losses and latency spikes that are hard to distinguish from operational events such as misconfigurations, transient congestion, or software regressions. Consequently, upon an adverse incident detection, support engineers must rapidly determine whether to route the corresponding incident ticket to network maintenance or escalate it to security operations. This triage phase represents a critical human-in-the-loop bottleneck in the incident response lifecycle. To address this vulnerability, we introduce C-RE-ACT (Causal RE-ACTing agent), an automated agentic triage framework designed to generate actionable incident reports. C-RE-ACT starts constructing a Weighted Directed Acyclic Graph (WDAG) over O-RAN metrics using the Structural Agnostic Model (SAM). The resulting causal topology is encoded into a continuous soft token via a Graph Isomorphism Network (GIN) aligned with the language space of the Large Language Model (LLM) powering a ReAct agent. We evaluate C-RE-ACT on a physical, O-RAN-compliant testbed across 140 distinct performance-degradation experiments. Empirical results demonstrate the causal ranking isolates the correct root cause within the top three candidates in 89% of instances. Furthermore, graph soft-prompting improves LLM accuracy on causal-topology queries from 0.22 (text-only baseline) to 0.72. The autonomous agent achieves anomaly classification accuracies of 83% for delay anomalies and 84% for packet-loss anomalies.
overflow_list.summary_cn: C-RE-ACT：面向O-RAN的性能退化攻击自动化研判框架。利用SAM构建O-RAN指标加权有向无环图（WDAG），经GIN编码后作为LLM ReAct agent的软提示词。在140个物理O-RAN测试床实验中，根因定位Top-3命中率达89%；图软提示使因果拓扑查询准确率从0.22提升至0.72；延迟异常分类83%，丢包异常84%。

strengths: Novel integration of causal discovery (SAM) + graph encoding (GIN) + LLM ReAct agent for O-RAN triage
Physical O-RAN-compliant testbed evaluation (140 experiments) with strong empirical rigor
Addresses a genuine operational bottleneck: human-in-the-loop triage delay in incident response
Caual ranking hits top-3 in 89% of cases; graph soft-prompting dramatically improves LLM accuracy from 0.22 to 0.72
End-to-end agentic pipeline from causal graph to actionable incident reports
limitations: SAM causal discovery quality not independently validated; relies on SAM assumptions
LLM accuracy on causal topology queries (0.72) still moderate; room for improvement
Single LLM model tested; generalizability to other LLMs unclear
Anomaly classification accuracy (83-84%) not exceptional for binary classification tasks
WDAG construction complexity and scalability for large O-RAN deployments not addressed
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Physical O-RAN testbed with 140 distinct performance-degradation experiments; real hardware, not simulation. Baselines include text-only LLM and BM25/vector retrieval methods.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Strong practical motivation, solid empirical validation on physical testbed, novel causal-graph-LLM integration. Slight concern that 0.72 LLM accuracy on causal queries is modest and the 83-84% classification is not state-of-the-art-level for binary tasks. Overall a solid, well-motivated contribution with clear deployment relevance.

overflow_list.title: Reliability- and Connectivity-Constrained Age-of-Information Optimization for UAV Swarm IoT Data Collection
overflow_list.authors: Milad Bafarassat, Sinem Coleri
overflow_list.abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle~(UAV) swarms provide a flexible platform for Internet of Things~(IoT) data collection by gathering delay-sensitive measurements from distributed sensor clusters and relaying them to a fusion center. Such missions require jointly optimizing data freshness, short-packet communication reliability, and swarm connectivity, yet existing approaches typically prioritize freshness while neglecting its impact on connectivity. This paper proposes a topology-coupled urgency~(TCU) scheduler that weights each cluster's age-of-information urgency by a per-UAV connectivity score, prioritizing stale clusters while dispersing collection across the swarm, with connectivity preserved by an explicit probabilistic constraint. For each time slot, the resulting problem is a mixed-integer nonconvex program, which we solve by successive convex approximation: the binary assignments are relaxed and the finite-blocklength rate, the inter-UAV link reliability and the connectivity score are linearized together into one convex subproblem, so their coupling is retained rather than broken across alternating blocks. Integer assignments are recovered by Hungarian matching and verified against the original nonconvex constraints, while a deficit queue sustains long-run coverage without explicit long-horizon planning. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheduler consistently achieves the lowest mean AoI and the highest service reliability among all baselines, reducing service failures by approximately $3.5\times$ under nominal operating conditions. Under increasingly stringent connectivity and coverage requirements, it maintains full service while competing methods either become infeasible or fragment the swarm, demonstrating the effectiveness of jointly optimizing data freshness, communication reliability, and connectivity.
overflow_list.summary_cn: TCU调度器：无人机蜂群物联网数据采集的拓扑耦合紧迫性调度方案。将数据新鲜度与节点连通性联合优化——按连通性评分加权各簇Age-of-Information紧迫性，优先处理陈旧簇同时保持全蜂群覆盖。通过连续凸近似+匈牙利匹配求解混合整数非凸问题。标称条件下平均AoI最低、可靠性最高，服务失败率降低约3.5倍；严苛连通需求下仍保持全服务，而基线方法失效或导致蜂群碎片化。

strengths: Joint optimization of AoI, reliability, and connectivity — addresses a real multi-objective gap in UAV swarm literature
TCU scheduler with connectivity score is intuitive and well-motivated
