Successive convex approximation retaining coupling across blocks (finite-blocklength rate, link reliability, connectivity) is methodologically sound
Deficit queue for long-run coverage is a practical engineering addition
3.5x reduction in service failures under nominal conditions; full service maintenance under stringent requirements
Hungarian matching for integer recovery with constraint verification
limitations: Simulation only; no experimental UAV swarm validation
Algorithm complexity for large swarms (scalability with UAV count) not analyzed
Deficit queue parameters appear heuristic; optimal tuning not addressed
Connectivity score definition not deeply validated — depends on how it is computed
Comparison baselines (likely state-of-the-art scheduling policies) not named or well-described
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Simulation-based evaluation. UAV swarm scenario with distributed sensor clusters and fusion center. Baselines are unnamed 'competing methods' from the literature. No real UAV flight data or hardware-in-the-loop experiments.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Solid optimization framework addressing a real multi-objective challenge in UAV swarms. The joint treatment of AoI, reliability, and connectivity is the main contribution; the specific algorithmic choices (convex approximation, Hungarian matching) are competent but not novel in isolation. Impact is good for UAV IoT data collection scenarios. Simulation-only evaluation limits confidence in practical deployment.

overflow_list.title: Wireless Imaging for Low-Altitude Surveillance: A New Paradigm for ISAC Networks
overflow_list.authors: Yixuan Huang, Jie Yang, Chao-Kai Wen, Shi Jin
overflow_list.abstract: The rapid growth of the low-altitude economy calls for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks capable of robust flight monitoring. This article advocates wireless imaging as a unifying sensing paradigm that enables ISAC networks to function as comprehensive low-altitude guardians. We present a hierarchical imaging framework that enhances sensing capability from wide-area snapshot imaging to dynamic trajectory-aware imaging and target-centric fine-grained characterization. At the wide-area level, low-altitude sensing is reformulated as a spatial imaging problem, where distributed base stations and communication users collaboratively construct a holistic view of the aerial space. Building on this foundation, multi-frame dynamic imaging exploits temporal correlations to support robust trajectory tracking and prediction under mobility induced challenges such as occlusions. For security-critical scenarios, the framework further enables fine-grained imaging of flying and hovering uncrewed aerial vehicles, providing detailed characterization beyond conventional point-target abstractions. Additionally, we propose a novel evaluation metric named imaging coverage to examine the sensing fidelity of the proposed framework. Illustrative case studies demonstrate the potential of imaging in ISAC networks to support wide-area monitoring, motion-aware tracking, and fine-grained target analysis.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 本文首次对商用VLP Wi-Fi 6E/7设备与5G NR（n102频段，40 MHz/30 kHz子载波间隔）的实际干扰进行传导测量。使用OpenAirInterface SDR平台搭建完整O-RAN/SDR栈，扫描Wi-Fi注入功率并记录gNB上行与UE下行吞吐量、误块率及信噪比。两接收机在-75 dBm以下均无可测性能降；高于此门限时性能逐步恶化。UE在低速率下更具鲁棒性，且不受仅信标传输影响。链路预算分析表明：VLP设备需与受害接收机距离远小于LBT exclusion zone（545–685 m），确认合规VLP设备将在干扰发生前完成信道释放。

strengths: Hierarchical imaging framework (wide-area snapshot → trajectory-aware → target-centric) is a genuinely novel organizing principle for ISAC
Reframing low-altitude sensing as spatial imaging rather than point-target estimation is a valuable conceptual contribution
Fine-grained UAV characterization beyond point-target abstraction addresses a real gap in UAV detection literature
Imaging coverage metric introduced as a sensing fidelity measure is a useful new evaluation lens
Addresses practical low-altitude economy surveillance need with clear application relevance
limitations: Case studies are illustrative but not comprehensive; limited diversity in drone types, BS deployments, and environmental conditions
No hardware validation or over-the-air experiments; results appear primarily analytical/simulation-based
Multi-frame dynamic imaging temporal correlation assumptions may not hold under severe occlusions or high-speed flight
BS-user collaboration mechanism for holistic aerial view construction lacks detailed protocol or overhead analysis
Security-critical fine-grained imaging claims are asserted without adversarial robustness analysis
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Case study-based evaluation with analytical and simulation results; no experimental or measurement data. Scenarios are limited to a few representative configurations rather than comprehensive parameter sweeps.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Novel paradigm paper that reframes ISAC sensing as imaging; likely to gain traction in ISAC and UAV detection communities. The hierarchical framework provides a structured way to think about sensing granularity across applications. Cited for conceptual framing even if detailed results are limited.

overflow_list.title: High-Altitude Platform Station-Aided Terahertz Satellite Communication Systems with Hardware Impairments
overflow_list.authors: Evla Safahan Ahrazoglu, Eylem Erdogan, Ibrahim Altunbas
overflow_list.abstract: The utilization of terahertz (THz) frequencies in satellite-aerial-ground communication systems stands out as a promising solution to accomplish both global connectivity and extreme data rates requirements of the sixth-generation networks. In the current literature, the impact of non-ideal equipment on the performance of THz satellite-aerial-ground communication systems remains unexplored, which is critical for practical implementations. Hence, this paper analyzes the performance of high-altitude platform station (HAPS)-aided THz satellite communication system in the presence of $α$-$μ$ fading, pointing errors, absorption loss, and hardware impairments for different atmospheric conditions. In the system of interest, it is assumed that variable-gain amplify-and-forward protocol is utilized at HAPS nodes (systems), and the HAPS system, which provides the maximum end-to-end signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), is selected for transmission. To evaluate the outage, asymptotic outage, and ergodic capacity bounds for the system, the probability density function, cumulative distribution function (CDF), and asymptotic CDF related to the upper bound of the end-to-end SNR are obtained. By using these statistics, the effects of hardware impairment levels, zenith angles, and atmospheric conditions on the system performance are examined. The results have shown that hardware impairments cause power loss in outage performance and reduce the system capacity. Moreover, it is demonstrated that the outage probability depends on either fading or pointing error characteristics in high SNR region and also that the system performance almost remains the same for lower zenith angles in HAPS-to-ground link regardless of the atmospheric conditions.
overflow_list.summary_cn: HAPS辅助太赫兹卫星通信系统性能分析。考虑α-μ衰落、指向误差、吸收损耗和硬件损伤，在不同大气条件下推导中断概率、渐近中断和遍历容量闭式界。结论：硬件损伤导致功率损耗并降低容量；高SNR区中断概率取决于衰落或指向误差特性；低天顶角下HAPS-地面链路性能对大气条件不敏感。

strengths: First analysis of HAPS-aided THz satellite systems with hardware impairments and α-μ fading
Comprehensive channel model including pointing errors, absorption loss, atmospheric conditions
Derives PDF, CDF, and asymptotic CDF for end-to-end SNR — mathematically rigorous
Variable-gain AF protocol with best-HAPS selection is practically relevant
Examines effects across zenith angles and atmospheric conditions
limitations: Purely theoretical/analytical; no hardware implementation or testbed validation
No comparison with prior HAPS-THz works (likely none exist, but still limits context)
Ergodic capacity and outage probability analysis is standard derivation technique; novelty in the application domain only
Assumptions about fixed-gain/ideal equipment may not hold in emerging THz hardware
Practical THz systems are not yet mature enough for real-world validation of findings
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Theoretical analysis only. No real or simulated system data. Derivation-based paper relying on established probability theory results applied to the specific channel model.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Solid mathematical derivation in an emerging domain, but the contribution is primarily application of known techniques to a new scenario. Low data score reflects no empirical validation. Impact is moderate because THz and HAPS are active research areas but practical deployment is years away. This is a competent theoretical paper rather than a breakthrough.

overflow_list.title: 6G: From Connectivity Infrastructure to Guaranteed Digital Services
overflow_list.authors: David Soldani, Petrit Nahi, Awn Muhammad, Nikhil Dwivedi, Francesco Monaco, Francis Jebamani
overflow_list.abstract: Sixth-generation mobile networks are approaching a structural inflection point. Five generations of vendor-led architecture have left operators dependent on platforms they cannot fully modify and artificial-intelligence inference layers they cannot audit. This article argues that 6G should reverse that trajectory by reordering five priorities: control first; customer outcomes before peak rates; business guarantees before megabytes; software-driven operations with governed agentic artificial intelligence; and technology in service of those priorities. Four contributions operationalize the thesis. The Control Compact is an own-federate-consume taxonomy that allocates architectural sovereignty by strategic value. The Guarantee Economy is a six-tier outcome-priced model aligned with IMT-2030 usage scenarios and converts operator control into enforceable service-level objectives. An operator-grade Network MCP Platform shows how autonomous agents could enter the service-based architecture through a governed tool plane with auditable hooks for identity, charging, lawful intercept, enforcement, and digital-twin validation. A standardization section states Rakuten Mobile's public position on AI-agent scope, radio access, migration, non-terrestrial networks, physical layer, core, and spectrum. The framework distinguishes operational evidence from national-scale cloud-native Open RAN and core network deployments, standards-grounded extrapolation, and forward-looking architecture and commercial proposals. A three-phase roadmap separates standards milestones from operator deployment targets and identifies validation gates and stakeholder implications.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 六代移动网络正面临结构性拐点。五代 vendor 主导的架构使运营商依赖无法完全修改的平台和无法审计的 AI 推理层。本文主张重排五大优先级：控制优先、客户成果先于峰值速率、业务保障先于流量、软件驱动运营搭配可治理的 AI Agent、技术服务于上述目标。提出四项贡献：Control Compact 分类法分配架构主权；Guarantee Economy 六层结果定价模型；运营商级 Network MCP 平台；Rakuten Mobile 的 AI Agent 标准化立场。三阶段路线图区分标准里程碑与部署目标。

strengths: Novel Control Compact taxonomy (own-federate-consume) provides actionable architectural sovereignty framework
Guarantee Economy six-tier model bridges IMT-2030 scenarios with commercial monetisation
Operator-grade Network MCP Platform addresses real AI-agent integration concerns (audit, charging, lawful intercept)
Rakuten Mobile's public standardization positions add credibility and industry relevance
Three-phase roadmap with validation gates provides actionable deployment path
limitations: Position paper lacks experimental validation; all proposals are extrapolations
No quantitative evaluation of Control Compact or Guarantee Economy performance
Network MCP Platform discussion is architectural, not implemented or tested
Business model sections lack revenue projections or cost-benefit analysis
Limited technical depth on AI-agent autonomy boundaries and governance mechanisms
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: No experimental data; paper is a standards-grounded position/extrapolation piece from a major operator. Assertions rest on Rakuten's operational experience rather than controlled studies.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Strong industry positioning and novel commercial frameworks; however, lack of experimental validation and quantitative rigor limits score. High practical impact as operator-driven 6G vision.

overflow_list.title: Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces Assisted UAV Communications
overflow_list.authors: Chandan Kumar Sheemar, Giovanni Iacovelli, Sourabh Solanki, Wali Ullah Khan, Symeon Chatzinotas
overflow_list.abstract: In this paper, we investigate an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communication system assisted by stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs), which enable programmable wave-domain signal processing through multiple cascaded metasurface layers. By shifting part of the beamforming functionality from the RF/digital domain to the electromagnetic domain, SIMs allow the realization of energy-efficient hybrid beamforming architectures suitable for aerial platforms. We formulate the joint design of digital precoding, SIM phase configuration, and UAV positioning for multi-user downlink sum-rate maximization. To solve the resulting non-convex problem, we develop an alternating optimization framework that guarantees monotonic improvement of the objective. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed SIM-assisted architecture significantly improves spectral efficiency while maintaining low hardware complexity, and highlight the impact of the number of metasurface layers and size of each layer on system performance.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 本文研究堆叠式智能超表面（SIMs）辅助无人机通信系统，通过多层级联超表面实现可编程波域信号处理。SIM 将部分波束赋形功能从射频/数字域转移至电磁域，实现适合无人机平台的高能效混合波束赋形架构。联合优化数字预编码、SIM 相位配置和无人机定位以最大化多用户下行总速率，采用交替优化框架保证目标单调提升。仿真表明 SIM 辅助架构显著提升频谱效率，同时降低硬件复杂度，并揭示了超表面层数和尺寸对性能的影响。

strengths: SIM (cascaded metasurface layers) is architecturally novel for UAV platforms—shifts beamforming to EM domain
Energy-efficient hybrid beamforming is critical for aerial platforms with strict power budgets
Alternating optimization with monotonic improvement guarantee provides convergence assurance
Joint digital precoding + SIM configuration + UAV positioning is comprehensive system design
Trade-off between metasurface layers/size and spectral efficiency is systematically characterised
limitations: SIM hardware implementation complexity and cost not discussed
Cascaded metasurface loss (insertion loss) may degrade practical performance vs. simulation model
UAV trajectory assumed static/slow-moving; high-mobility scenarios not addressed
No comparison with conventional RIS-assisted or fully-digital beamforming baselines
Phase-only control assumption for SIM elements may not hold with real metasurface hardware
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Numerical simulations with standard channel models. No experimental hardware prototype. Performance trade-offs explored across multiple SIM configurations. Moderate data quality typical of theoretical communication papers.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Innovative SIM-assisted UAV communication concept with solid optimization framework. Monotonic AO convergence is a strength. Novelty is high (EM-domain beamforming shift). Practical impact depends on SIM hardware maturity. Would benefit from hardware-in-the-loop validation.

overflow_list.title: TRUAV: Distributed Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Trajectory Planning and Routing Enhancement in UAV-Aided IoT-Enabled VANETs
overflow_list.authors: Muhammad Umar Farooq Qaisar, Lin Zhang, Zhen Chen, Wajdy Othman, Shehzad Ashraf Chaudhry, Chang Liu
overflow_list.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have emerged as a key enabler of next-generation Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems, offering flexible aerial relaying to extend connectivity across dynamic vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) in smart city environments. However, conventional centralized approaches for UAV trajectory planning require continuous global network state aggregation, making them impractical under bandwidth and energy constraints typical of dense urban deployments. In this article, we present TRUAV, a distributed multi-agent reinforcement learning framework based on independent tabular Q-learning for joint UAV trajectory planning and routing enhancement in UAV-aided VANETs. Each UAV is equipped with a local Q-learning agent that operates purely on locally observable information, including vehicle density, packet queue states, and neighbor UAV positions, thereby eliminating the need for global state exchange. A potential-game-inspired reward design encourages spatial diversity and routing-aware UAV positioning among interacting agents while accounting for energy consumption. Numerical simulations over a large urban area with 200 mobile vehicles show that the proposed TRUAV framework achieves network coverage and packet delivery ratios comparable to centralized deep reinforcement learning methods, while also improving relay delay and energy efficiency. Finally, we discuss emerging challenges and future research directions for distributed multi-agent UAV-assisted IoT systems.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 本文提出 TRUAV，一种基于独立表格 Q-learning 的分布式多智能体强化学习框架，用于无人机辅助车联网的联合轨迹规划与路由优化。每架无人机仅基于本地可观测信息（车辆密度、数据包队列状态、邻居无人机位置）运行，无需全局状态交换。基于潜在博弈的奖励设计促进空间多样性和路由感知定位。仿真表明 TRUAV 在覆盖率、交付率上媲美集中式深度强化学习方法，同时降低中继时延、提升能效。

strengths: Distributed MARL approach eliminates global state aggregation bottleneck—practical for bandwidth-constrained VANETs
Potential-game reward design elegantly couples spatial diversity with routing objectives
Local Q-learning enables true on-device computation without centralised controller
Compares against centralised DRL baselines, not just trivial heuristics
Addresses energy efficiency alongside communication performance
limitations: Tabular Q-learning may not scale to large state spaces in denser deployments
Only 200 vehicles in simulation—larger-scale urban scenarios untested
Reward function design (potential game) not formally proven to converge to Nash equilibrium
Synthetic mobility models; no real-world VANET trace validation
UAV energy consumption model appears simplified (hover vs. mobility trade-off underexplored)
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Numerical simulations on synthetic urban scenarios with 200 vehicles. No real-world datasets. Baselines include DQN and DDPG variants, providing reasonable comparison class.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Solid distributed RL contribution with practical relevance for UAV-assisted VANETs. Moderate novelty (combines existing techniques). Rigor is adequate for a simulation study. Would benefit from larger-scale evaluation and formal convergence analysis.

overflow_list.title: Analysis of UAV-Enabled IoT Networks with Energy Harvesting and Wake-Up Radio
overflow_list.authors: Anthony Khairallah, Nour Kouzayha, Tareq Y. Al-Naffouri, Hadi Sarieddeen
overflow_list.abstract: This paper investigates an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled Internet of Things (IoT) architecture that integrates wake-up radio (WuR) and energy harvesting for sustainable device operation. In the proposed system, UAVs transmit radio-frequency (RF) signals that both trigger device activation and replenish stored energy. The IoT device's behavior is modeled as a discrete-time Markov chain, which captures the evolution of its battery level and operational state (asleep or awake), accounting for both energy harvesting and energy consumption. Leveraging stochastic geometry and discrete-time Markov-chain analysis, we develop a comprehensive mathematical framework to assess system performance. We reveal a tradeoff between transmission frequency and energy consumption, and demonstrate that tuning of system parameters, such as UAV density, can significantly improve both energy efficiency and transmission reliability.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 本文研究了一种集成唤醒收音机（WuR）和能量采集的无人机（UAV）辅助物联网架构。无人机发射射频信号，同时触发设备激活并补充存储能量。物联网设备的行为被建模为离散时间马尔可夫链，捕捉电池电量和工作状态（休眠或唤醒）的演化。基于随机几何和马尔可夫链分析，构建了全面的数学框架评估系统性能，揭示了传输频率与能耗之间的权衡。

strengths: Integrates three sustainability mechanisms (WuR + EH + UAV) in a unified framework — timely for energy-constrained IoT
DTMC modeling of joint battery level and sleep/awake state is appropriate and captures the coupled dynamics well
Stochastic geometry for UAV density analysis provides useful system-level insight
Reveals clear transmission-frequency vs. energy-consumption tradeoff — actionable design guideline
Good identification of practical deployment knobs (UAV density tuning)
limitations: Relies entirely on simulations; no real hardware or testbed validation
Markov chain assumption (geometric inter-arrival, i.i.d. harvesting) may not capture correlated shadowing or bursty traffic in real UAV-IoT channels
WuR activation probability model is simplified; does not account for false wake-ups or capture failure under interference
No discussion of UAV trajectory, hovering energy cost, or mobility management — significant omissions for a UAV paper
Limited discussion of how harvested energy is split between activation vs. storage replenishment
Baseline comparisons (when included) appear to be heuristic, not state-of-the-art
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Purely simulation-based evaluation with synthetic traffic and channel models. No real dataset or hardware-in-the-loop validation. Assumptions (fixed harvest rate, simple path loss) are reasonable but untested against measured UAV-to-ground RF transfer data.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Solid stochastic modeling foundation with a practically relevant tradeoff finding. Deductions primarily on the absence of real-world validation and incomplete UAV-specific modeling (trajectory, hover energy). Likely to receive moderate interest in UAV-IoT and energy-harvesting communities but may be viewed as preliminary without testbed results.

overflow_list.title: ISAC-Enabled On-Demand UAV Charging for Wireless Rechargeable Sensor Networks
overflow_list.authors: Muhammad Umar Farooq Qaisar, Lin Zhang, Paolo Bellavista, Shehzad Ashraf Chaudhry, Shamsher Ullah, Chang Liu
overflow_list.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with wireless power transfer (WPT) extend the lifetime of wireless rechargeable sensor networks (WRSNs) by delivering energy on demand. This article presents an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC)-enabled on-demand UAV charging framework coordinated by a central base station. A prioritized charging queue captures node urgency and service cost through residual energy, traffic load, estimated UAV travel time, and flight-direction alignment. This bidirectional coupling ensures that scheduling decisions shape the UAV trajectory, while updated mobility estimates from ISAC dynamically reorder the queue. ISAC-assisted estimation of UAV distance, speed, and position updates travel-time predictions under mobility uncertainty. A time-allocated partial charging policy distributes limited hover time across queued nodes according to criticality. Simulations show gains in energy usage efficiency, travel distance, and charging delay compared with representative baselines. We discuss deployment considerations, including computational overhead, scalability, and parameter selection, to aid practitioners evaluating the framework for IoT scenarios.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 配备无线功率传输（WPT）的无人机可按需为无线可充电传感网络（WRSN）提供能量，延长网络寿命。本文提出一种集成感知通信（ISAC）辅助的按需无人机充电框架，由中央基站协调调度。通过残存能量、业务负载、无人机飞行时间估计和飞行方向对齐等因素构建优先级充电队列，实现调度决策与无人机轨迹的双向耦合。ISAC辅助估计无人机距离、速度和位置以更新行程时间预测。

strengths: ISAC + on-demand UAV charging is a compelling and timely combination — sensing enables smarter scheduling
Bidirectional coupling between scheduling and trajectory (queue ↔ UAV mobility) is a genuine contribution that goes beyond decoupled approaches
Prioritized charging queue captures urgency through multiple factors (residual energy, traffic load, travel time, flight alignment) — realistic multi-dimensional priority
Time-allocated partial charging policy addresses the practical constraint of limited hover time
Discussion of deployment considerations (computational overhead, scalability) adds practical value beyond the simulation results
Comparisons with representative baselines demonstrate clear performance gains in energy efficiency, travel distance, and charging delay
limitations: Centralized coordination by a single base station may create a single point of failure and scalability bottleneck for large IoT deployments
ISAC estimation accuracy (UAV distance, speed, position) under non-line-of-sight or adverse weather is not deeply analyzed
Partial charging policy assumes known urgency and does not address adversarial or noisy priority input
Simulation parameters (UAV speed, hover time, IoT node density) appear synthetic; no calibration against real UAV platforms or deployment data
The V2I communication model supporting ISAC estimation is not detailed — channel models, latency requirements, and interference not characterized
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Simulation-based with synthetic network topologies and mobility traces. Travel-time predictions and ISAC estimation errors are modeled rather than measured. No real UAV flight data or operational WRSN dataset. Gains are relative to baselines but absolute performance in field conditions is uncertain.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Strong conceptual novelty with the bidirectional scheduling-trajectory coupling and ISAC-assisted mobility estimation. Practical impact is high for UAV charging in WRSNs. Deductions for centralized architecture scalability concerns and lack of real-world dataset validation. Expected to be well-received in UAV-wireless and ISAC communities, with potential as a foundations paper for integrated sensing and wireless power transfer.

overflow_list.title: AI-Empowered UAV-Assisted Backscatter Localization and ISAC for Zero-Energy IoT: A Comprehensive Survey
overflow_list.authors: Ruhul Amin Khalil
overflow_list.abstract: Zero-energy Internet of Things (IoT) enables passive or near-passive devices to operate on harvested energy rather than batteries. Backscatter communication (BackCom) supports this vision by enabling tags to transmit data via reflection and modulation of incident RF signals, but it suffers from weak reflections, double-path loss, limited coverage, direct-link interference, and dependence on external RF sources. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can mitigate these limitations by acting as mobile carrier emitters, data collectors, relays, aerial receivers, mobile anchors, sensing platforms, and edge-intelligence nodes. Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) further enables the sharing of wireless resources for data transmission, localization, target sensing, and environmental awareness. This article surveys RF-based AI-empowered UAV-assisted backscatter localization and ISAC for zero-energy IoT. It reviews enabling technologies, presents a structured PRISMA-informed methodology, and develops a unified taxonomy covering network architectures, UAV roles, backscatter modes, RF sources, localization and sensing functions, AI techniques, and performance metrics. It also discusses UAV-assisted BackCom, passive localization, ISAC-enabled UAV-backscatter systems, and AI-driven optimization through comparative tables, quantitative trend analysis, coverage evaluation, and tutorial-style numerical illustrations. Finally, it identifies open challenges and future directions in realistic channel modeling, energy-neutral operation, benchmarking, reproducibility, scalable and trustworthy AI, security, privacy, hardware validation, and integration with RIS, MEC, digital twins, and 6G technologies.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 本文综述面向零能耗物联网的射频AI赋能无人机辅助反向散射定位与通感一体化（ISAC）技术。文章建立统一分类体系，涵盖网络架构、无人机角色及AI技术，分析使能技术，并通过定量分析与实例评估探讨系统性能，最后指出信道建模、安全隐私及与6G融合等未来挑战。

strengths: First comprehensive survey integrating AI, UAV, backscatter, ISAC, and zero-energy IoT under one taxonomy
PRISMA-informed methodology with structured literature review across multiple dimensions
Rich comparative tables, quantitative trend analysis, and coverage evaluation
Extensive coverage of UAV roles (carrier, relay, anchor, sensing platform, edge node)
Forward-looking discussion of open challenges: realistic channel modeling, energy-neutrality, benchmarking, security
limitations: Survey without new empirical results; all findings are synthesized from existing literature
AI techniques covered broadly but not deeply evaluated for specific backscatter/ISAC scenarios
Hardware validation section is aspirational rather than empirical
Integration discussions (RIS, MEC, DT, 6G) remain at conceptual level without concrete protocol designs
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Comprehensive survey covering UAV-backscatter localization and ISAC literature; comparative tables and quantitative trends are informative but sourced from heterogeneous prior work with varying evaluation conditions.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: High-quality comprehensive survey well-suited for IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials or similar venues. Strong relevance to 6G UAV and ISAC topics; limited by survey-only nature but excellent for establishing taxonomy and research roadmap.

overflow_list.title: Learning to Compute on Dirty Paper
overflow_list.authors: Shreesal Shrestha, Kuranage Roche Rayan Ranasinghe, Giuseppe Thadeu Freitas de Abreu, Elza Erkip
overflow_list.abstract: We propose a fully learning-based approach to integrated communication and computing (ICC) that combines dirty paper coding (DPC) with over-the-air computation. Each user employs a neural encoder with sinusoidal activations that learns to pre-cancel its own computing symbol as non-causally known interference, recovering modulo-like periodic structures consistent with lattice-based DPC schemes. A joint neural decoder recovers all users' messages from the received signal, while a separate neural AirComp estimator exploits a multi-slot block structure to estimate a target function of the computing symbols after the encoder-decoder network converges. To our knowledge, this is the first fully learning-based approach to jointly address DPC-based interference pre-cancellation and over-the-air computation in a unified framework.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 本文提出结合脏纸编码(DPC)与无线计算的联合通信与计算(ICC)全学习框架。每个用户使用具有正弦激活的神经编码器学习预抵消自身计算符号，联合神经解码器从接收信号恢复所有用户消息，独立神经网络AirComp估计器利用多时隙块结构估计计算符号的目标函数。这是首个统一解决DPC干扰预抵消与无线计算的端到端学习方法。

strengths: First fully learning-based approach combining dirty paper coding with over-the-air computation in unified framework
Neural encoder with sinusoidal activations cleverly captures modulo-like periodic structures of lattice-based DPC
Joint neural decoder and separate AirComp estimator architecture is well-designed
Addresses fundamental theoretical problem with practical learning-based solution
limitations: Likely simulation-only evaluation; unclear if realistic channel models and interference scenarios tested
Neural DPC may not achieve theoretical capacity of optimal DPC; performance gap not characterized
Training convergence and computational complexity not discussed in abstract
Practical deployment challenges such as channel estimation errors and synchronization not addressed
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Abstract lacks details on evaluation dataset; likely synthetic simulation-based experiments
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Highly novel theoretical contribution bridging DPC and AirComp, but practical validation appears limited

overflow_list.title: From RAN Control to Agentic Intelligence: Architecture and Vision for Energy Efficient AI-RAN
overflow_list.authors: Sabrine Aroua, Alexis I. Aravanis, Ilias Chatzistefanidis, Hamza Abbar, Anh-Khoa Dang, Anastasios Giovanidis, Salah-Eddine El Ayoubi, Stephane Senecal, Martha Vlachou Konchylaki, Navid Nikaein
overflow_list.abstract: Future 6G networks will rely on highly distributed, AI-native Radio Access Networks (RANs), where communication and AI workloads share a common infrastructure. This evolution, combined with increasing deployment density and continuous AI processing, is expected to significantly increase RAN energy consumption. While Open RAN (O-RAN) introduces a programmable and modular control framework through the RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) and Service Management and Orchestration (SMO), current approaches remain largely policy-driven, limiting adaptive energy-aware coordination across multiple applications. In parallel, AI-RAN promotes the convergence of AI and RAN infrastructures through AI-for-RAN, AI-on-RAN, and AI-and-RAN paradigms, yet efficient mechanisms to jointly orchestrate performance, latency, and energy remain an open challenge. This article proposes an agentic AI-native RAN architecture that bridges O-RAN's structured control with AI-RAN's unified vision. Leveraging semantic intent abstraction and Large Language Model (LLM)-driven coordination, the framework enables adaptive orchestration, conflict resolution, and energy-aware multi-objective optimization across heterogeneous workloads. Through representative AI-for-RAN and AI-on-RAN use cases, we show how such coordination can improve resource efficiency and reduce operational energy consumption, paving the way toward sustainable 6G networks.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 未来6G网络将依赖高度分布式、AI原生的无线接入网（RAN），通信和AI工作负载共享基础设施。本文提出一种代理式AI原生RAN架构，结合O-RAN的结构化控制与AI-RAN的统一愿景，利用语义意图抽象和大语言模型（LLM）驱动的协调机制，实现跨异构工作负载的自适应编排、冲突解决和能效多目标优化，为可持续6G网络铺平道路。

strengths: Timely topic: energy efficiency in AI-RAN is a critical and open 6G challenge
Novel framing: bridging O-RAN's structured control with AI-RAN's unified vision through semantic intent abstraction
LLM-driven coordination for conflict resolution is a fresh architectural contribution
Multi-objective optimization across performance/latency/energy is well-motivated
Use cases (AI-for-RAN and AI-on-RAN) concretize the architecture
limitations: Mostly architectural/visionary; no mathematical formulation or formal analysis of the energy tradeoffs
Use case results appear illustrative rather than rigorous comparative evaluation
LLM integration introduces inference latency and cost not quantified
No clear benchmark against existing O-RAN RIC energy management approaches
Multi-objective optimization claim not validated with concrete metrics or Pareto analysis
Scalability of LLM coordination to large-scale deployments unclear
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Architecture and use case analysis only; no real-world dataset; no simulation parameters or numerical results beyond high-level claims; 3GPP baseline absent.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Strong novelty and timely motivation with a compelling architectural vision, but limited rigor (largely conceptual) and absent quantitative evaluation of energy savings or coordination performance reduce confidence in practical claims.

overflow_list.title: Adaptive 5G Resource Allocation for Multistatic ISAC-Based UAV Detection and Tracking
overflow_list.authors: Cole Dickerson, Wahab Khawaja, Ismail Guvenc
overflow_list.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) enable numerous commercial and public-safety applications, yet they also create security risks near critical infrastructure, transportation hubs, and restricted airspace. While integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) can leverage existing wireless networks for UAV surveillance, practical deployment must address competition between sensing and communication demands, as well as the challenges associated with tracking highly maneuverable UAVs with low radar cross section (RCS). This paper investigates adaptive multistatic ISAC for load-aware UAV detection and tracking in 5G wireless networks. A shared-resource framework is developed to quantify how sensing waveform length, sensing transmission rate, and beam allocation affect communication throughput in a 5G new radio (NR) system. Detection performance is analyzed using Zadoff-Chu (ZC) sensing waveforms, while tracking continuity is evaluated through an M-of-N detection model. To improve robustness under congestion, software-defined sensor (SDS) nodes exploit external signals of opportunity (SoO) to provide supplemental passive sensing opportunities when network resources become limited. Results show that adaptive sensing policies outperform fixed sensing reservations by preserving throughput under dynamic load while maintaining useful sensing capability. Under heavy congestion, SDS assistance substantially reduces tracking outage in the simulated scenarios. Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) analysis demonstrates that multistatic sensing geometries improve localization accuracy and provide more uniform spatial coverage than monostatic sensing alone. These results highlight coordinated adaptive sensing and distributed multistatic support as a practical path toward resilient UAV surveillance in future wireless networks.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 本文研究5G网络中自适应多基地通感一体化（ISAC）用于无人机检测与跟踪。提出共享资源框架量化感知对通信吞吐量的影响，并利用软件定义传感器节点在拥塞时利用外源信号辅助感知。结果表明，自适应感知策略在保持通信性能的同时维持了感知能力，多基地几何结构显著提升了定位精度。

strengths: Adaptive multistatic ISAC framework for UAV surveillance in 5G NR with shared-resource trade-off analysis
Zadoff-Chu sensing waveforms with M-of-N detection model — practical and well-established
Software-defined sensor (SDS) nodes exploiting signals of opportunity under congestion is a practically valuable robustness mechanism
CRLB analysis quantifies localization accuracy improvement from multistatic geometry over monostatic baseline
Realistic congestion scenarios demonstrate adaptive sensing policy advantages over fixed reservations
limitations: Results are simulation-based; no hardware prototype or over-the-air experimental validation
SDS node behavior and SoO selection strategy could be more rigorously characterized
UAV maneuver model appears simplified; high-maneuver scenarios under low-RCS conditions not deeply explored
Resource allocation algorithm complexity not evaluated against 5G NR real-time processing constraints
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Simulation-based evaluation with 5G NR system parameters; CRLB analysis provides theoretical lower bounds. SDS assistance evaluated under simulated congestion conditions with controlled load variations.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Strong practical contribution for 5G UAV surveillance; well-suited for 5G/6G ISAC venues. CRLB analysis adds rigor; SDS concept is novel and practically valuable. Would benefit from over-the-air validation and complexity analysis to strengthen acceptance at top-tier wireless conferences.

overflow_list.title: ConsisFormer: Compute-Efficient Transformer for Wireless Foundation Models Based on Channel Consistency
overflow_list.authors: Yuwei Wang, Li Sun, Tingting Yang, Liwen Jing, Yuxuan Shi, Maged Elkashlan, Mérouane Debbah
overflow_list.abstract: Wireless foundation models (WFMs) have recently emerged as a promising paradigm for AI-native 6G networks, enabling universal channel representations adaptable to diverse communication and sensing tasks. Existing WFMs are predominantly built upon the Transformer architecture, which delivers superior performance but incurs computational complexity proportional to the square of the input sequence length, posing a significant barrier to their deployment under stringent inference latency constraints. To address this issue, in this paper, we propose ConsisFormer, a compute-efficient Transformer design based on short-term consistency of wireless channels, as a WFM backbone. By utilizing the observation that adjacent time or frequency instances share similar clusters of scatterers and thus exhibit similar channel characteristics, we develop an adaptive token aggregation (ATA) module to dynamically merge neighboring channel state information (CSI) tokens, thereby reducing the length of the token sequence involved in self-attention calculations to lower the computational cost. Furthermore, we propose a feature sequence interpolation (FSI) method to recover the full CSI representation based on the sparse feature sequence outputted from the Transformer blocks, thus keeping the performance unaffected while ensuring low complexity. Moreover, we propose an aggregated auto-encoder (AAE) pre-training paradigm for WFMs, enabling robust channel representation learning from sparsified CSI tokens via compression and recovery. Simulation results show that the proposed design reduces the computational complexity of WFM by over $83\%$ with negligible performance loss on various tasks including channel prediction, LoS/NLOS classification, beam prediction, and localization.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 无线基础模型（WFM）是AI原生6G网络的关键范式，但现有Transformer架构计算复杂度高。本文提出ConsisFormer，一种基于无线信道短期一致性的高效Transformer。利用相邻时频实例信道特性相似的特点，引入自适应令牌聚合模块降低序列长度，并提出特征序列插值恢复完整表征。此外，设计了聚合自编码器预训练范式。仿真表明，该方法在各项任务性能损失极小的情况下，计算复杂度降低超83%。

quality_assessment.strengths: Novel compute-efficient Transformer design leveraging wireless channel short-term consistency; Adaptive token aggregation reduces computational complexity by over 83% with negligible performance loss; Aggregated auto-encoder pre-training paradigm for robust channel representation learning; Comprehensive evaluation across multiple tasks (channel prediction, LoS/NLOS classification, beam prediction, localization)
quality_assessment.limitations: Short-term consistency assumption may not hold in high-mobility or rapidly changing channel conditions; Performance evaluation limited to simulation; real-world deployment challenges not addressed; Comparison with other efficiency techniques (pruning, quantization) not provided; Token aggregation strategy may introduce latency in dynamic environments
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Simulation-based evaluation across diverse tasks; no real-world dataset validation; performance metrics comprehensive but synthetic
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: High novelty in wireless-specific Transformer optimization; strong empirical results with significant complexity reduction; practical impact depends on real-world validation and deployment in actual 6G systems

overflow_list.title: Wind-Resilient Trajectory Optimization for UAV-BS Networks: TD3 for Continuous Service Availability
overflow_list.authors: Azim Akhtarshenas, German Svistunov, Kuangyu Zheng, David Lopez-Perez
overflow_list.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-mounted base stations are highly susceptible to wind disturbances such as gusts and turbulence, which induce positional drift and degrade communication link quality, particularly in emergency scenarios. To address this challenge, we propose a DRL-based framework for wind-resilient trajectory adjustment and positioning based on the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm. The method models wind as a stochastic kinematic perturbation, avoiding complex aerodynamic modeling, thereby enabling the TD3 agent to learn adaptive control policies that maintain optimal coverage footprints. By prioritizing user-centric performance metrics under turbulent conditions, the proposed architecture ensures continuous service availability despite external disruptions. Simulation results demonstrate that the TD3-based approach effectively compensates for wind-induced displacements and outperforms benchmark methods, including Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), in terms of throughput stability and robustness in windy environments.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 无人机基站易受风扰导致位置漂移与通信质量下降。本文提出基于TD3算法的深度强化学习框架，实现抗风轨迹调整与定位。该方法将风建模为随机运动扰动，使智能体学习自适应控制策略以维持最佳覆盖。仿真结果表明，该方法有效补偿风致位移，在吞吐量稳定性与鲁棒性上优于PPO等基准方法。

strengths: Wind-resilient trajectory optimization is a practically relevant problem for UAV-BS deployment in emergency scenarios
Wind modeled as stochastic kinematic perturbation avoids complex aerodynamics—pragmatic design choice
Clear comparison with PPO shows TD3 advantages in throughput stability under windy conditions
limitations: Incremental contribution: TD3 for UAV trajectory under wind is a straightforward application of an existing DRL algorithm with no architectural novelty
Wind model is extremely simplified (stochastic kinematic perturbation)—no gust profiles, turbulence models, or real wind data used
No real-world validation, real wind traces, or even hardware-in-the-loop testing; pure toy simulation
User-centric metric design is under-specified—coverage footprint optimization details are vague
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: No real data whatsoever. Wind modeled as a simple stochastic perturbation in simulation. No standard wind datasets (e.g., NREL, meteorological records) used. Evaluation is entirely in a controlled, simplified simulation environment.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: This paper applies a standard DRL algorithm (TD3) to a well-studied problem (UAV trajectory optimization) with simplified wind assumptions and no real-world validation. The contribution is too incremental for a strong venue.

overflow_list.title: Time-Slotted Multi-Cluster UAV AirComp with Energy-Awareness: A Pointer Network-Assisted Soft Actor-Critic Learning Framework
overflow_list.authors: Xunqiang Lan, Xiao Tang, Ruonan Zhang, Qinghe Du, Tony Q. S. Quek
overflow_list.affiliations: School of Electronics and Information | Northwestern Polytechnical University, Xi’an.(lanxun | Pillar, Singapore University of Technology and Design, Singapore | Singapore.(
overflow_list.abstract: Over-the-air computation (AirComp) has emerged as a promising approach for massive data aggregation, which is yet challenged by the channel variations, task distributions, and inherent energy limitation of the computation nodes. In this paper, we propose an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted Aircomp system to serve multi-cluster computation tasks over time, where the UAV mobility-facilitated spatial and time diversity is exploited for efficient and accurate data computation. Specifically, we aim for the minimization of AirComp aggregation error and the energy consumption by jointly optimizing the transceiver beamforming, normalizing factors, sensor scheduling, and UAV trajectory. To solve the formulated problem, we decompose it into two layers where the inner layer addresses the optimization-based AirComp transceiver design, and the outer layer focuses on the deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based scheduling and trajectory design. In particular, a pointer network actor-critic learning is developed to tackle the binary scheduling problem, and a soft actor-critic DRL algorithm is employed to determine the UAV trajectory. Simulation results validate the convergence of the proposed hierarchical learning framework and demonstrate its significant performance gains in terms of AirComp aggregation error and energy consumption as compared with baseline schemes.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 空中计算（AirComp）是大规模数据聚合的有前景方案，但受信道变化、任务分布和节点固有的能量限制挑战。本文提出UAV辅助的AirComp系统，利用UAV移动性带来的空间和时间分集服务多集群计算任务，通过联合优化收发波束成形、归一化因子、传感器调度和UAV轨迹，最小化聚合误差和能耗。采用分层学习框架求解，内层处理基于优化的收发设计，外层采用深度强化学习进行调度和轨迹设计。

strengths: Hierarchical decomposition (inner: optimization-based transceiver design; outer: DRL scheduling/trajectory) is a principled and well-motivated problem structuring
Pointer network + soft actor-critic combination is novel for UAV AirComp; effectively handles both discrete scheduling and continuous trajectory
Joint optimization of beamforming, normalizing factors, sensor scheduling, and UAV trajectory is comprehensive
Mobility-facilitated spatial and time diversity exploitation is a meaningful system insight
Simulation results validate convergence of the framework — important for DRL stability claim
limitations: Fully simulation-based; no real UAV experiments, no SDR or hardware validation
UAV energy model and number of sensor nodes/clusters not clearly characterized
Baseline comparison schemes not fully specified; may be setting up a strawman
Generalization: does the learned policy transfer to different environments or task distributions?
AirComp theory assumes synchronized channel estimation which may not hold in practice
Computation complexity of pointer network actor-critic at scale not discussed
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Simulation-based evaluation with synthetic/semi-realistic channel models; aggregation error and energy consumption are well-defined metrics; scale of simulation (number of sensors, clusters, UAVs) not clearly specified.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Technically strong with a novel combination of tools (pointer network + SAC) applied to a well-defined problem. Moderate data quality (simulation-only) and practical deployment barriers (synchronization assumptions) prevent a higher score, but the hierarchical approach is sound and the results are convincing within the simulated setting.

overflow_list.title: UAV-CAS: A Calibrated Digital-Twin Dataset for Intrusion Detection in UAV Swarm Networks
overflow_list.authors: Sripath Mishra, Bharat Bhargava, Zizheng Liu, Shafkat Islam
overflow_list.abstract: Intrusion detection systems (IDS) trained on wired-network benchmarks degrade sharply in real-world unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms, where mobility, fluctuating link quality, and decentralized routing reshape traffic distributions. Existing UAV-specific datasets also do not systematically vary these conditions, leaving no way to train or test an IDS against the very shift that defeats it. We present UAV-CAS, a large-scale labeled flow dataset for UAV-network intrusion detection, generated by a Containernet digital twin that is systematically calibrated against AERPAW testbed measurements. We have a four-layer calibration pipeline spanning altitude-dependent path loss, mission-specific mobility, the link-level performance chain, and end-to-end trace fidelity. UAV-CAS comprises 99,492 flows drawn from 1,024 configurations that span five attack families (DoS, DDoS, blackhole, wormhole, replay) and nine collaborative attack compositions. A diversity analysis shows that high-rate attacks separate from benign traffic up to an order of magnitude more strongly than in any prior benchmark, while stealth attacks deliberately blend with benign traffic. Across ten baseline IDS, binary attack detection saturates above $0.98$, confirming the dataset is learnable, whereas full attack-class identification remains hard -- per-class $F_1$ ranges from near zero to $0.82$ and falls into the single digits for stealth attacks. We release the dataset, simulator, and calibration data to support reproducible UAV intrusion-detection research.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 基于有线网络基准训练的入侵检测系统（IDS）在无人机集群中性能急剧下降。现有数据集缺乏对移动性、链路质量等条件的系统变化。我们提出UAV-CAS，一个大规模标注流数据集，通过Containernet数字孪生生成，并经AERPAW测试台校准。数据集包含99,492条流，涵盖五类攻击和九种协同攻击组合。分析显示高流量攻击区分度高，而隐蔽攻击难以识别。十种基线IDS测试表明二分类检测率超0.98，但细粒度攻击识别仍具挑战。

strengths: First systematically calibrated digital-twin dataset for UAV intrusion detection with four-layer calibration pipeline
Large-scale dataset (99,492 flows, 1,024 configurations) spanning five attack families and nine collaborative attack compositions
Diversity analysis shows high-rate attacks separate from benign traffic up to order of magnitude more strongly than prior benchmarks
Comprehensive baseline evaluation across ten IDS models with clear performance gaps identified for stealth attacks
limitations: Containernet simulation may not fully capture all real-world UAV swarm dynamics and hardware constraints
Attack detection saturates above 0.98 but full attack-class identification remains challenging (F1 ranges near zero to 0.82)
Dataset focused on network-layer attacks; physical-layer and cross-layer attacks not addressed
Calibration against AERPAW testbed limited to specific scenarios; generalization to other UAV platforms unclear
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Real testbed calibration (AERPAW) with systematic four-layer pipeline; large-scale synthetic data with controlled variation; comprehensive baseline comparisons
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Strong novelty in calibrated digital-twin methodology for UAV IDS; rigorous calibration and evaluation; practical impact limited by simulation-to-reality gap and focus on network-layer attacks

overflow_list.title: Communication Channel Modelling of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
overflow_list.authors: Necati Kagan Erkek, Emre Balcı, Berkin Halay, Hakan Ali Çırpan
overflow_list.affiliations: BİLGEM Hisar Laboratory personnel for their
overflow_list.abstract: Wireless communication channel characterization for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is essential for reliable control, data transmission, and mission performance in civil, industrial, and defence applications. Channel behaviour is examined using a measurement-based approach that captures both large-scale propagation effects, represented by path loss, and small-scale characteristics, represented by the channel impulse response (CIR) and power delay profile (PDP). An SDR-based channel sounding system is employed to collect and process in-phase and quadrature (IQ) data, enabling the extraction of key channel parameters. Following system verification, measurements are conducted in ground-to-ground (G2G), air-to-ground (A2G), and air-to-air (A2A) scenarios. The results demonstrate that path loss alone is insufficient to describe UAV communication channels, as CIR and PDP provide additional insight into multipath propagation and delay-domain behaviour. The findings indicate that realistic UAV channel models should incorporate both large-scale and small-scale channel statistics. Further improvements may be achieved through increased sounding bandwidth, enhanced synchronization, measurements in a wider range of environments, and more detailed analysis of Doppler effects.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 无人机（UAV）无线通信信道建模对民用、工业和国防领域的可靠控制、数据传输和任务执行至关重要。本研究采用基于SDR的信道探测系统，通过测量方法分析大尺度传播效应（路径损耗）和小尺度特性（信道冲激响应CIR和功率时延谱PDP）。在地面到地面（G2G）、空对地（A2G）和空对空（A2A）场景下进行测量，结果表明仅靠路径损耗不足以描述UAV通信信道，CIR和PDP能提供多径传播和时延域行为的额外洞察。研究建议未来UAV信道模型应同时纳入大尺度和小尺度统计特性。

strengths: Three scenario categories (G2G/A2G/A2A) provide useful comparative channel insights
SDR-based IQ data collection is a sound and reproducible measurement approach
Correctly identifies that large-scale path loss alone is insufficient for UAV channel modeling — an important and well-supported conclusion
Clear, well-structured presentation accessible to practitioners
limitations: Incremental over prior UAV channel measurement campaigns; methodology (SDR sounding + CIR/PDP extraction) is established in literature
Unclear scale of measurements: number of measurement runs, environments, distances, frequency bands not specified
No real-world dataset link provided; reproducibility unclear
Practical impact limited: no deployment guidance, no specific model parameters, no link to 3GPP or standardization
Doppler and mobility effects acknowledged but not analyzed in detail
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Measurement-based with SDR collection, but scale and environmental diversity unspecified; no public dataset; 3GPP channel models not used as baseline comparison.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Solid empirical measurement work with a correct and non-obvious insight (path loss insufficient), but incremental over prior art, underspecified measurement scale, and limited practical/deployment guidance.

overflow_list.title: Towards Ubiquitous 6G Computing and Networking Convergence: Architecture and Mechanism for Cross-Domain Resource Coordination
overflow_list.authors: Yang Li, Xing Zhang, Yan Zhang, Wenbo Wang
overflow_list.affiliations: School of Information and Communications Engineering, Beijing University | School of Information and Communication Engi | • A comprehensive survey of existing research efforts on | CNC is conducted, revealing current research gaps | • Potential challenges and future research directions are
overflow_list.abstract: The 6G network will support six major application scenarios, such as immersive communication, integrated AI and communication, and integrated sensing and communication. Many scenarios necessitate significant computational support. Moreover, user demands are becoming increasingly segmented, diverse, and personalized. Traditional network slicing alone is insufficient to meet the heterogeneous computing and networking demands of emerging service scenarios. Mobile computing network convergence (CNC) introduces a fundamentally different paradigm from the conventional cloud computing plus communication network model by deeply embedding computing resources into the mobile network infrastructure and enabling integrated computing-network services tailored to diverse user demands. In this article, we investigate orchestration architectures and mechanisms for CNC in 6G mobile networks. We begin by reviewing the evolution of CNC from a mobile network perspective and surveying existing studies, which we categorize according to mobile network architectures. Building on these insights, we propose a hierarchical, cross-domain coordination architecture and an orchestration mechanism based on hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning. Performance evaluations demonstrate that the proposed architecture and mechanism significantly reduce system energy consumption while enhancing task satisfaction rate. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future research directions.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 6G网络支持沉浸式通信、AI通信融合、感知通信融合等六大场景，传统网络切片无法满足异构计算需求。移动计算网络融合(CNC)将计算资源嵌入移动网络基础设施，提供定制化服务。本文提出分层跨域协调架构和基于分层多智能体强化学习的编排机制，显著降低能耗并提高任务满意度。

strengths: Comprehensive survey and categorization of computing-network convergence (CNC) evolution from a mobile network perspective
Hierarchical cross-domain coordination architecture addresses real 6G challenges of heterogeneous resource management
Multi-agent reinforcement learning approach is well-motivated for distributed coordination problems
Strong practical relevance to emerging 6G scenarios requiring integrated computing and networking
limitations: Simulation details are limited in the abstract; unclear if realistic network topologies and traffic models were used
Hierarchical MARL can suffer from scalability issues and training instability in large-scale deployments
Energy consumption and task satisfaction metrics may not capture full complexity of CNC trade-offs
Comparison with baseline orchestration schemes needs more detail
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Performance evaluation mentioned but dataset scale and realism unclear from abstract; likely simulation-based
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Strong architectural contribution with industry relevance, but methodology rigor and data quality appear moderate based on abstract

overflow_list.title: Digital Twin-Based Channel Generation Toolchain and Foundation Model for Low-Altitude XL-MIMO
overflow_list.authors: Mengyuan Li, Yu Han, Jiachen Tian, Chao-Kai Wen, Shi Jin
overflow_list.abstract: The rapid development of the low-altitude economy (LAE) has created growing demand for reliable aerial communication systems. Extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) is a promising enabler for such systems due to its high spatial resolution and robust connectivity. However, three-dimensional (3D) mobility together with near-field propagation makes it difficult to obtain dedicated high-fidelity wireless datasets, hindering systematic algorithm development and evaluation. To address this issue, we develop LAETwin-XL, a digital twin (DT)-based toolchain and dataset for XL-MIMO research in LAE scenarios. Built on the Sionna ray-tracing (RT) module, the proposed toolchain simulates near-field and far-field channels with diverse wireless labels for practical environments. Building on this dataset, we further develop a conditional denoising diffusion implicit model (CDDIM)-based generative foundation model that is pretrained to learn transferable XL-MIMO channel representations from incomplete channel observations. Unlike conventional task-specific or foundation models that rely on relatively complete channel inputs, the proposed model can generatively infer informative channel representations from partially observed channels. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves effective zero-shot channel extrapolation performance. Furthermore, using lightweight task heads and limited training data, it enables parameter-efficient transfer to various downstream tasks (e.g., channel estimation, classification, and localization), delivering high accuracy and robustness even under sparse antenna observations. The codes and dataset are available at https://github.com/Lmyxxn/LAETwin-XL.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 低空经济快速发展亟需可靠空通信系统。XL-MIMO虽具优势，但3D移动性与近场传播导致数据获取难。本文提出LAETwin-XL工具链与数据集，基于Sionna模拟信道，并开发生成式基础模型，能从不完整观测推断信道表征。实验表明该框架实现有效零样本外推，在稀疏天线观测下高效迁移至下游任务，兼具高精度与鲁棒性。

strengths: Novel integration of digital twin (Sionna RT) with conditional diffusion model for XL-MIMO channel generation in low-altitude scenarios
Zero-shot channel extrapolation from partial observations via CDDIM is a practically valuable capability
Well-structured toolchain (LAETwin-XL) with open-sourced code and dataset on GitHub
limitations: Entirely synthetic data—ray-tracing from Sionna, no real-world over-the-air validation or measured channel data
CDDIM architecture is a known class of diffusion models; core generative methodology is not novel
Evaluation limited to simulated environments; generalization to unseen real-world LAE topologies is untested
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Synthetic only (Sionna RT simulation). Dataset is released, which is good, but no real-world measurement or experimental validation is provided.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: The toolchain is a solid engineering contribution for LAE XL-MIMO research, and the generative extrapolation idea is clever, but the paper remains 100% simulation-based without experimental validation, capping its overall impact.

overflow_list.title: Active Perception for Radio Map Reconstruction in Uncharted 3D Air-Ground Environments
overflow_list.authors: Wenlihan Lu, Miaowen Wen, Shijian Gao
overflow_list.abstract: Radio maps provide the essential foundation for low altitude networking systems. Unlike terrestrial radio maps that are typically generated via drive test measurements, mapping the air-ground environment requires the deployment of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). This shift introduces two formidable challenges in uncharted 3D scenarios. First, sparse radio measurements and incomplete geometric observations hinder accurate reconstruction. Second, the large 3D action space and strict power constraints from high spectrum scanner energy consumption make informative exploration difficult. To address these issues, this paper proposes 3D uncertainty aware radio active mapping (3D-URAM), a closed loop active perception framework that decouples the mapping process into two offline trained stages. In Stage I, a Bayesian UNet is developed to recover radio maps from sparse measurements and partial geometry while providing calibrated predictive uncertainty. In Stage II, a dynamic probabilistic roadmap and a transformer based waypoint selection policy trained via proximal policy optimization maximize long horizon uncertainty reduction under travel budgets. Experimental results demonstrate that 3D-URAM reduces reconstruction error by over 50% compared to representative baselines. Real-world field tests within a 300mx200mx100m space also validate the potential of active radio map reconstruction.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 无线电地图是低空网络的基础。针对无人机测绘中稀疏测量与高能耗探索的挑战，本文提出3D-URAM闭环主动感知框架。该框架分两阶段：利用贝叶斯UNet重建地图并提供不确定性，结合动态概率路图优化航点选择。实验表明，该方法重建误差降低超50%，实地测试验证了其有效性。

strengths: Closed-loop active perception framework (3D-URAM) that decouples Bayesian radio map reconstruction from transformer-based waypoint planning is a clean, novel architecture
Real-world field tests in a 300m×200m×100m space validate practical feasibility—rare in this domain
Achieves >50% reconstruction error reduction over representative baselines, a strong quantitative result
limitations: Bayesian UNet is a well-known architecture; core reconstruction methodology is not fundamentally new
Field test details are brief—hardware setup, flight time, measurement density are not deeply characterized
Transformer waypoint policy trained via PPO may not scale to much larger 3D spaces without retraining or curriculum learning
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Combines simulation training with real-world field tests in a substantial 3D volume. The field validation is commendable, though measurement density and ground-truth collection methodology could be reported more thoroughly.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Strong paper with real-world validation—rare for this space. The 50%+ improvement is compelling, and the problem (radio map reconstruction for uncharted 3D air-ground environments) is practically important for LAE deployment.

overflow_list.title: Modular Multi-Domain Digital Twin Architecture: Sustainable Intent-Driven 6G Management
overflow_list.authors: Berk Buzcu, Marcin Pakula, Gevher Yesevi Keskin, Laura Finarelli, Gianluca Rizzo, Engin Zeydan, Jorge Baranda, Aitor Alcazar-Fernandez, Javier Velazquez-Martinez, Luis M. Contreras, Gil Kedar, Efi Dvir, Paweł Kryszkiewicz
overflow_list.abstract: Future 6G networks will operate across distributed and heterogeneous domain infrastructures, making conventional single-domain management insufficient for proactive, trustworthy automation. Network Digital Twins (NDTs) enable what-if analysis, AI-assisted optimization, and risk-free validation of control actions before deployment, yet monolithic end-to-end twins remain impractical due to scalability, fidelity, and cross-domain coordination challenges. Accordingly, this paper proposes a Digital Twin-enabled 6G architecture that exposes NDT capabilities as a specialized service domain within a multi-domain orchestration framework built on a state-of-the-art service-based 6G architecture. A DT Orchestrator interprets \textit{predictive} and \textit{prescriptive} what-if queries and composes domain-specific DT modules and simulators on demand, while decision authority remains with the requesting entity. Furthermore, a generalized workflow covers telemetry synchronization, simulation-based decision support, and closed-loop execution. The framework is demonstrated through a green-networking use case that couples a system-level O-RAN cellular digital twin component with a two-stage solar-allocation simulator, evaluated over a 105-base-station deployment in Poznan using simulative datasets. Joint coverage and renewable optimization reduces daily grid consumption by 28.5\% with 32 solar panels at the diminishing-returns threshold, with 17 base stations identified as both coverage-active and high-priority solar candidates as evidence that cross-domain NDT coordination enables sustainable, intent-driven 6G network management.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 未来6G网络跨分布式异构域，传统单域管理不足。本文提出数字孪生使能的6G架构，将NDT能力作为多域编排框架中的服务域。编排器解析假设查询并按需组合模块，通过绿色网络用例验证：联合覆盖与可再生能源优化使日电网消耗降低28.5%，证明了跨域NDT协调可实现可持续、意图驱动的网络管理。

strengths: Architecture for multi-domain NDT orchestration with predictive/prescriptive what-if query interpretation is novel and well-designed for 6G intent-driven management
Concrete green-networking use case evaluated over a 105-BS real deployment in Poznan with quantitative energy savings (28.5% grid reduction)
Generalized workflow covering telemetry sync, simulation-based decision support, and closed-loop execution—practically useful framework
limitations: Evaluation uses 'simulative datasets' rather than real telemetry from the 105 BS sites—data realism is uncertain
Solar allocation (two-stage simulator) is a relatively simple validation use case; more complex cross-domain scenarios would strengthen the proposal
The architecture introduces a DT Orchestrator but decision authority and privacy-preserving cross-domain data sharing mechanisms are not deeply addressed
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Uses simulative datasets based on a real 105-BS deployment in Poznan, which is better than pure synthetic. However, relying on simulated rather than measured telemetry data limits the strength of the quantitative claims.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: A well-architected paper with a clear vision for multi-domain NDT coordination. The green-networking use case with 28.5% grid reduction is compelling. The main weakness is reliance on simulative data rather than real telemetry, but the architecture itself is a solid contribution to 6G management.

overflow_list.title: Temporally Consistent Graph Q-Networks for Intelligent Network Control
overflow_list.authors: Zacharias Veiksaar, Maxime Bouton
overflow_list.affiliations: Work done while at Ericsson Research, Sweden. Ericsson Research
overflow_list.abstract: Mobile networks continue to grow in complexity and next generation networks are expected to support both increasing traffic loads and more diverse services. As network complexity rises, optimizing antenna parameters under dynamic or changing objectives becomes increasingly challenging. We propose a novel multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) algorithm for high-level control and orchestration of mobile networks.   The Temporally Consistent Graph Q-Network (TC-GQN) algorithm learns a self-predicting representation of the whole network that is task-independent and aggregates information from all base-stations. A graph neural network is trained using a global reward function to assign coordinated local actions based on the learned encoding of the global network state. We evaluate the algorithm in a simulated environment to orchestrate an energy-saving feature across multiple sectors and multiple carriers under different quality of service (QoS) constraints. The proposed algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art graph-based baselines and a competitive rule-based controller by improving hardware sleep time while maintaining QoS. Moreover, the learned representation enables rapid adaptation to changing intents.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 本文提出时间一致性图Q网络(TC-GQN)算法，用于移动网络的高层控制与编排。该算法学习任务无关的全局自预测表示，图神经网络通过全局奖励函数协调多基站本地动作。在模拟环境中评估能效节省功能，在不同QoS约束下优于现有方法，提高硬件休眠时间同时保持服务质量，学习到的表示支持快速适应变化意图。

strengths: Self-predicting task-independent representation enables rapid adaptation to changing objectives
Graph neural network architecture naturally captures base-station coordination structure
Practical energy-saving use case with QoS constraints demonstrates real-world applicability
Outperforms both graph-based baselines and rule-based controllers with meaningful metrics
limitations: Simulation environment details unclear; may not capture full complexity of real RAN deployments
Global reward function may be difficult to design and tune for diverse network objectives
Multi-agent RL training stability and sample efficiency challenges not fully addressed
Hardware sleep time metric may not translate directly to actual energy savings in practice
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Simulated environment with practical metrics; reasonable for algorithm development but not real deployment
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Strong algorithmic contribution with practical motivation and competitive results, though simulation-based evaluation limits immediate impact

overflow_list.title: LLM-Enabled NWDAF: A Step Toward AI-Native 6G Network Intelligence
overflow_list.authors: Henok Daniel, Omar Alhussein, Cheng Li, Jie Liang, Ernesto Damiani
overflow_list.affiliations: School of Engineering Science, Simon Fraser University, Vancouver, Canada | Center of Cyber Physical Systems(C2PS), Department of Computer Science, Khalifa University, Abu Dhabi, UAE
overflow_list.abstract: The Network Data Analytics Function (NWDAF) is central to enabling zero-touch network management in fifth-generation (5G) networks by supporting real-time analytics and closed-loop automation. Despite its critical role, open-source NWDAF implementations remain limited in scope and accessibility. In this paper, we develop an open-source NWDAF, compatible with the open-source core network Free5GC, that collects network data via subscriptions to Network Functions (NFs), and also includes an integrated Large Language Model (LLM) interface that enables natural language interaction with human operators. The interface processes user intents, encodes them using a semantic embedding model, and maps them to one of seven predefined intent categories to trigger analytics queries or event subscription commands. This architecture abstracts the complexity of traditional interfaces, allowing non-expert users to manage network analytics and subscriptions with ease. The system supports Access and Management Function (AMF) and Session Management Function (SMF) event subscriptions, real-time monitoring, and analytics retrieval via Prometheus, all accessible through a conversational interface. By bridging AI-driven intent recognition with standardized network analytics, our implementation enhances operator usability and provides a foundation towards AI-native 6G networks. The source code and datasets generated during the current study are available in the github repository, https://github.com/HenokDanielbfg/testbed.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 网络数据分析功能(NWDAF)是5G零触网络管理的核心，支持实时分析和闭环自动化。本文开发了兼容Free5GC的开源NWDAF，集成了大语言模型接口实现自然语言交互，可处理用户意图并映射到预定义类别触发分析查询。系统支持AMF和SMF事件订阅、实时监控和Prometheus分析检索，为AI原生6G网络奠定基础。

strengths: Open-source NWDAF implementation fills important gap in 5G/6G research infrastructure
LLM-based natural language interface for network management is timely and innovative
Integration with Free5GC and Prometheus demonstrates practical system-building capability
Seven predefined intent categories provide structured approach to intent-based networking
limitations: Limited to AMF and SMF event subscriptions; does not cover full NWDAF analytics scope per 3GPP specs
Intent classification into seven predefined categories may be restrictive for complex operator queries
LLM interface adds latency and potential reliability concerns for time-critical network operations
Evaluation focuses on functionality; performance under load and scalability not demonstrated
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Real implementation with generated datasets available on GitHub; practical but limited scale evaluation
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Valuable open-source contribution with practical LLM integration, but scope is limited and evaluation depth is moderate

overflow_list.title: Towards Intelligent Wireless Networks: The Synergy of Generative AI and Digital Twins
overflow_list.authors: Afan Ali, Ali Arshad Nasir, Naveed Iqbal, Daniel Benevides da Costa
overflow_list.abstract: This paper proposes a generative AI (GenAI)-enabled digital twin (DT) framework for proactive and energy-aware wireless optimization in future 6G ecosystems. Most existing AI-assisted DT approaches remain fundamentally reactive, adjusting network parameters only after performance degradation occurs or restricting GenAI to isolated signal-level tasks such as channel estimation. This work adopts a proactive approach. Instead of responding to problems after they appear, the proposed framework continuously synchronizes channel states, mobility dynamics, traffic conditions, and energy information within a real-time DT environment, enabling the system to anticipate congestion, interference, and energy demand before they materialize. The result is a closed-loop proactive architecture that operates at the system level, jointly managing communication, mobility, and resource dynamics for autonomous wireless control. Evaluations on a UAV-assisted non-terrestrial network (NTN) scenario show approximately 69.2\% energy savings over reactive baselines while maintaining reliable quality-of-service (QoS) under dense and mobility-intensive conditions. Beyond this specific scenario, the framework offers a scalable foundation for broader AI-native 6G applications, including aerial platforms, autonomous systems, extended reality (XR), industrial automation, and space-air-ground-sea (SAGS) integrated infrastructures.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 本文提出一种生成式AI赋能的数字孪生框架，用于6G网络的前瞻性能量感知优化。不同于现有被动响应方法，该框架通过实时同步信道、移动性及能量信息，提前预测拥塞与干扰，实现闭环主动控制。在无人机辅助非地面网络场景评估中，该框架在保证服务质量的同时，较被动基准节能约69.2%，并为AI原生6G应用提供了可扩展的基础架构。

strengths: Proactive GenAI-enabled digital twin framework for wireless optimization; significant energy savings (69.2%) demonstrated in UAV-assisted NTN scenario; Closed-loop architecture jointly managing communication, mobility, and resources; Scalable foundation for broader AI-native 6G applications
limitations: Framework novelty limited as GenAI-DT integration conceptually straightforward; Energy savings claim based on single UAV-NTN scenario; generalization unclear; GenAI component details and model architecture not thoroughly described; Reactive baseline comparison may not represent state-of-the-art proactive approaches
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Simulation-based evaluation in UAV-NTN scenario; energy savings quantified but QoS metrics less detailed; no comparison with other proactive optimization methods
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Good novelty in proactive GenAI-DT integration; practical energy savings demonstrated; impact depends on broader validation across diverse 6G scenarios and clearer GenAI methodology

overflow_list.title: AI-Native Closed-Loop Security for 6G-Enabled Cyber-Physical Systems: From Edge Detection to Network-Wide Mitigation
overflow_list.authors: Bilal Hussain, Muhammad Bilal, Tan Li, Haris Pervaiz, Xiao Tang, Qinghe Du, Fawad Ahmad, Muhammad Azhar, Jun Zhang
overflow_list.abstract: In sixth-generation (6G) networks, billions of cyber-physical systems (CPSs) - autonomous vehicles, smart grids, industrial robots, and remote-surgical equipment - will run over ultra-reliable low-latency slices, collapsing the gap between a remote breach and physical harm to milliseconds, a budget perimeter firewalls and centralised security operations centres cannot meet. This survey reframes 6G CPS security as a closed-loop, AI-native pipeline that senses at the multi-access edge computing (MEC) tier, using minute-scale call-detail records (CDRs) for baseline learning and sub-millisecond RAN/Open-RAN (O-RAN) telemetry for the latency-critical path. It decides locally with compressed deep models, mitigates network-wide via SDN, NFV, and O-RAN controllers, and retrains through federated learning (FL) and digital-twin (DT) replay. We formalise a per-slice, tail-bounded latency contract on the sense, detect, and mitigate stages, enforced at a slice-dependent tail percentile (p99 for safety-critical URLLC slices). Organising 128 peer-reviewed studies (2017-2026) under a PRISMA 2020 protocol, we (i) map the 6G/CPS threat surface to MITRE ATT&CK and a CDR-observable feature space; (ii) unify edge anomaly detection and DDoS classification across twelve datasets and statistical, graph, and transformer models; (iii) synthesise SDN/NFV/O-RAN primitives into one closed-loop reference architecture; (iv) treat FL, large language models (LLMs), DT, post-quantum cryptography (PQC), zero-trust architecture (ZTA), and explainable AI as cross-cutting enablers, not parallel pillars; and (v) consolidate open problems into five directions spanning data, latency, trust, standardisation, and evaluation.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 本文综述6G网络中信息物理系统（CPS）的安全问题，提出闭环AI原生安全管道，利用MEC感知、CDR基线学习和RAN遥测，结合SDN/NFV及联邦学习实现本地决策与全网缓解。研究确立了严格的时延契约，基于PRISMA协议分析128篇文献，映射威胁面，统一异常检测模型，整合参考架构，并指明数据、时延、信任等五大未来方向。

strengths: Comprehensive PRISMA 2020 survey of 128 studies bridging 6G/CPS security and AI-RAN
Novel threat-to-mitigation architecture unifying SDN/NFV/O-RAN controllers with MEC edge sensing
Practical threat mapping to MITRE ATT&CK with CDR-observable feature space
