Well-integrated treatment of FL, LLMs, DT, PQC, ZTA, and XAI as cross-cutting enablers rather than isolated pillars
Per-slice tail-bounded latency contract formalization addresses real deployment constraints
limitations: Survey nature limits direct empirical validation of proposed architecture
Weibull distribution assumption for latency contracts not universally validated across deployment scenarios
Federated learning and digital-twin components described at architecture level without detailed protocol specifications
O-RAN telemetry sub-millisecond requirement may be challenging in practical RAN deployments
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Synthesizes 12 datasets across edge anomaly detection and DDoS classification; strong breadth but heterogeneous evaluation conditions across the 128 studies limit direct comparability.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Survey with strong practical framing for 6G CPS deployment; architectural contribution is high-value synthesis but limited by survey-only evaluation methodology. Likely high acceptance at 6G/security venues given timeliness of the closed-loop security topic.

overflow_list.title: Mitigating Anchoring Bias in LLM-Based Agents for Energy-Efficient 6G Autonomous Networks
overflow_list.authors: Hatim Chergui, Claudia Carballo González, Farhad Rezazadeh, Merouane Debbah
overflow_list.abstract: This paper presents an autonomous agentic resource negotiation framework designed to enable zero-touch network slicing in 6G architectures using Large Language Model (LLM) agents. While LLMs offer powerful reasoning capabilities, we demonstrate that such agents inherently suffer from anchoring bias, rigidly adhering to initial heuristic proposals and causing severe network over-provisioning. To systematically mitigate this cognitive bias, we propose a novel randomized anchoring strategy modeled via a Truncated 3-Parameter Weibull distribution. This mathematically bounded approach seamlessly integrates with burst-aware Digital Twins (DTs) employing Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) to rigorously guarantee strict Service Level Agreement (SLA) tail-latencies. To validate our methodology, we introduce and prove the \emph{Bimodal Constraint-Avoidance Utility Theorem}, demonstrating that while feasible negotiations follow classical convex bounds, highly constrained scenarios undergo a phase transition governed by an inverse rational decay envelope. Empirical results generated using a locally hosted 1B-parameter model otel-llm-1b-it confirm these dual-regime bounds. Our cognitive de-biasing successfully dismantles rigid negotiation patterns, forcing agents into active exploration to safely ride SLA boundaries and boost system energy savings up to 25\%. Crucially, the lightweight 1B LLM achieves sub-second inference latencies (0.95s mean), ensuring our multi-agent framework is compatible with the operational timescales of the O-RAN non-Real-Time RAN Intelligent Controller (non-RT RIC)\footnote{Our source code is available for non-commercial use at https://github.com/HatimChergui.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 本文提出基于大语言模型（LLM）代理的自主资源协商框架，实现6G零接触网络切片。针对代理的锚定偏差问题，提出截断Weibull分布随机锚定策略，结合数字孪生与CVaR保障SLA尾时延。实验证明该方法打破僵化协商模式，提升系统节能25%，且轻量级LLM推理时延满足O-RAN非实时RIC要求。

strengths: Novel identification and rigorous mitigation of anchoring bias — a practically important cognitive bias in LLM-based network agents
Truncated 3-Parameter Weibull distribution provides mathematically sound, bounded randomization strategy
Bimodal Constraint-Avoidance Utility Theorem is a genuine theoretical contribution with phase-transition insight
CVaR + burst-aware DT integration addresses tail-latency SLA guarantees for URLLC-relevant scenarios
Lightweight 1B model (otel-llm-1b-it) with sub-second inference validated for O-RAN non-RT RIC timescales
25% energy savings claim substantiated by controlled experiments
limitations: Empirical validation uses a single 1B model; generalization to larger LLMs not explored
DT + CVaR overhead not clearly characterized against the reported inference latency budget
Burst modeling assumptions (Weibull parameters) may need tuning across different traffic patterns
No evaluation under adversarial or adversarial LLM inputs
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Simulation-based validation with locally hosted 1B model; results credible but limited to single-model evaluation. No comparison against alternative de-biasing strategies beyond the ablation implied by the anchoring strategy.
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Strong novelty in cognitive-bias mitigation for LLM agents; theoretically grounded with useful theorem; practical O-RAN non-RT RIC compatibility is a strong differentiator. Medium-high acceptance likely; would benefit from multi-model robustness validation and real-network traces.

overflow_list.title: RSMA Enabled Hierarchical UAV Networks with Non Linear Energy Harvesting: Outage Probability Analysis and UAV Placement Optimization
overflow_list.authors: Faicel Khennoufa, Khelil Abdellatif, Metin Ozturk, Halim Yanikomeroglu, Safwan Alfattani
overflow_list.abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) are expected to enhance connectivity, extend network coverage, and support advanced communication services in sixth-generation (6G) cellular networks, particularly in public and civil applications. Although multi-UAV systems offer greater efficiency and cost-effectiveness than single-UAV deployments, their implementation still faces several fundamental challenges that limit their reliability, sustainability, and scalability. The limited onboard energy restricts mission duration and communication continuity. Therefore, wireless energy harvesting (EH) emerges as a promising solution to overcome this limitation. However, terrestrial energy sources experience path loss, making EH from surrounding UAVs more sustainable. Moreover, rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) remains insufficiently explored in hierarchical UAV networks under hardware impairments (HWI) and imperfect channel state information (ICSI). This paper proposes a hierarchical ad hoc UAV network with non-linear EH and RSMA to enhance both energy and cost efficiency, where UAVs harvest energy from surrounding UAVs. For a practical scenario, we consider the effect of HWI and ICSI in our proposed system. To the best of the authors knowledge, this study is the first to investigate such a scenario in the literature. The outage probability expressions for ground Internet of things (IoT) devices, each CMU, and the overall outage probability of the proposed system are derived over Nakagami-$m$ fading channels while considering practical constraints such as HWI, ICSI, and non-linear EH. Additionally, approximate outage probability expressions are derived for high transmit power regimes. Subsequently, we formulate two optimization problems to enhance reliability and performance. Our findings indicate that the proposed system outperforms all benchmarks in terms of outage probability.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 无人机（UAV）将在6G网络中发挥关键作用，但多无人机系统受限于机载能量。无线能量收集（EH）是解决之道，且从邻近无人机收集能量更具可持续性。本文提出一种结合非线性EH和速率分割多址（RSMA）的分层自组网UAV网络，并在硬件损伤和非理想信道信息下推导了中断概率表达式。结果表明，该系统在中断概率方面优于所有基准，显著提升了可靠性和性能。

strengths: First study combining RSMA, non-linear EH, HWI, and ICSI in hierarchical UAV networks
Comprehensive analytical framework with closed-form outage probability expressions over Nakagami-m fading
Considers practical constraints including hardware impairments and imperfect CSI
Optimization formulations for reliability and performance enhancement
limitations: Purely analytical study without simulation or experimental validation of derived expressions
Non-linear energy harvesting model adds complexity but practical feasibility unclear
Assumptions about inter-UAV energy harvesting sustainability not validated with real-world data
Limited discussion on implementation complexity and signaling overhead for RSMA in UAV networks
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: No real or simulation data; purely theoretical derivations; validation through numerical examples only
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Moderate novelty in combining multiple techniques; rigorous analytical work but lacks empirical validation; practical impact uncertain without implementation evidence

overflow_list.title: A Novel Stripe-based RIS Optimization for UAV Communications and Sensing in Low-Altitude Wireless Networks
overflow_list.authors: Burak Ahmet Celebi, Sefa Kayraklik, Onur Salan, Ibrahim Hokelek, Ali Emre Pusane, Ali Gorcin
overflow_list.abstract: Low-altitude wireless networks (LAWN) envision a reconfigurable 3D network capable of supporting mission-critical aerial operations. This paper presents a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted LAWN to establish a reliable communication with an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) across varying wireless channel conditions and signal blockages. A low complexity stripe-based RIS phase shift optimization framework is proposed to simultaneously enhance communication reliability and provide passive sensing capability for UAV tracking under 3D mobility. Unlike high-complexity optimization approaches, the proposed method leverages the inherent structural phase-gradient of the RIS adjacent elements to significantly reduce the search space for calculating and updating the RIS configuration as the UAV moves. The analysis and simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms conventional benchmarks in convergence speed and computational efficiency, while maintaining robust, high signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) connectivity even in the presence of phase estimation errors and low SNR regimes. In addition, the measurement experiments using a real RIS prototype in an outdoor campus environment are performed to demonstrate the practical viability of the proposed approach.
overflow_list.summary_cn: 低空无线网络（LAWN）旨在支持关键空中任务。本文提出一种RIS辅助的LAWN，在信道变化和遮挡下建立可靠通信。提出低复杂度条纹式RIS相移优化框架，利用相邻元件的结构相位梯度减少搜索空间，同时增强通信可靠性与被动感知能力。仿真与室外原型实验表明，该方法在收敛速度和计算效率上优于传统基准，且在相位估计误差和低信噪比下仍保持稳健连接。

strengths: Low-complexity stripe-based RIS phase shift optimization leveraging structural phase-gradient; Simultaneous communication enhancement and passive sensing for UAV tracking; Real RIS prototype experiments in outdoor campus environment demonstrating practical viability; Robust performance under phase estimation errors and low SNR regimes
limitations: Stripe-based approach trades optimality for complexity; performance gap from optimal solution not quantified; Outdoor experiments limited to campus environment; scalability to dense UAV networks unclear; Passive sensing capability demonstrated but accuracy metrics limited; RIS prototype details and hardware constraints not thoroughly discussed
quality_assessment.data_quality_note: Combination of simulation analysis and real prototype experiments; outdoor validation adds practical credibility; dataset size and diversity not specified
quality_assessment.prediction_reason: Solid novelty in stripe-based RIS optimization; good balance of theory and experimentation; practical impact moderate due to complexity-optimality trade-off and limited experimental scope
